tools.name: growth_session_init
tools.description:
SINGLE session-start call — bundles auth state + external-tool detection (Clay / Crunchbase browser-cookie probes) + skill overrides + verbiflow browser-session probe into one response. Call this as the FIRST tool of every session before rendering anything to the user. Returns { auth, connected_tools, skill_overrides, browser: {verbiflow_signed_in} }.

`browser.verbiflow_signed_in` is a silent SQLite existence probe (no Keychain prompt) that detects whether the user is currently signed into *.verbiflow.com in any Chrome profile. Combine with auth.is_anonymous to decide whether the MCP session was lost vs. genuinely fresh:
  - is_anonymous=true AND verbiflow_signed_in=true → SUGGEST growth_relogin (strong signal: they have a real account, this MCP just lost its token).
  - is_anonymous=true AND verbiflow_signed_in=false → fresh anon user, route through normal claim flow at delivery (growth_claim_account_oauth).
  - is_anonymous=false → already authed, ignore the probe.

tools.name: growth_auth_status
tools.description: Report the current session: anonymous or claimed user, user_id, workspace slug, and the full list of workspaces the viewer belongs to (id, name, slug). Every skill flow should call this first. Use `workspaces` to name the destination when confirming sequence creation — and if length > 1, ask the user which workspace before calling growth_create_sequence_draft.

tools.name: growth_reset_session
tools.description: Nuke the MCP's local anon session and sign in fresh. Use when Supabase rejects the current tokens with "invalid JWT" / "signature invalid" — typically after a Supabase project JWT-key rotation. Creates a brand-new anonymous user; any previous unclaimed anon workspace is orphaned (Supabase sweeps them on its own schedule).

tools.name: growth_claim_account_oauth
tools.description: Preferred claim flow. Returns a one-click URL that hands this anonymous session to the browser and immediately starts Google (or Microsoft) OAuth. After sign-in, the OAuth identity attaches to the SAME user row, so the workspace / sequences / senders the MCP built carry over unchanged. Use this when the user needs to open the web builder or dashboard. Prefer this over growth_claim_account (magic-link) unless the user explicitly asks for email-based claim.

next_path.description: In-app path to land on after OAuth completes, e.g. "/w/my-workspace/sequences/seq_abc/builder". Must start with "/".

new_workspace_name.description: REQUIRED, non-empty. Display name for the new workspace — use the company name you researched the sequence for, e.g. "Acme Corp". The workspace is renamed to this on claim. Never pass an empty string.

new_workspace_domain.description: REQUIRED, non-empty. Company domain, e.g. "acme.com" — use the domain of the company you built the sequence for. The claim flow auto-enriches the workspace with the company logo, industry, and description (same as normal onboarding). Never pass an empty string.

tools.name: growth_claim_account
tools.description: Attach an email to the current anonymous user. Supabase sends a magic link to the provided email; on click, the anonymous user becomes a real user with that email — workspace, sequences, and senders all carry over with no migration. Idempotent: already-claimed users get a fresh magic link. Returns a claim_token the agent can poll via growth_check_claim_status to detect when the user actually clicks the link.

email.description: Email address to bind to this account. Must be a real mailbox the user can check right now.

tools.name: growth_check_claim_status
tools.description: Poll the status of a claim_token returned by growth_claim_account_oauth or growth_claim_account. Returns { status: "pending" | "claimed" | "expired", minted_at, claimed_at?, claimed_user_id?, claimed_email? }. Use this to wait for the user to finish OAuth or click their magic link without asking them to confirm. Poll roughly every 20-30s; stop on "claimed" or "expired".

claim_token.description: The claim_token uuid returned by growth_claim_account_oauth or growth_claim_account.

tools.name: growth_relogin
tools.description:
Re-authenticate a user whose MCP session was previously real (claimed) but whose tokens got invalidated server-side (Supabase JWT key rotation, manual revoke, refresh window blown). Returns a one-click URL the user opens; the page does Google/Microsoft OAuth (not linkIdentity), grabs the resulting Supabase session for their EXISTING auth.users row, mints a per-user MCP token, and POSTs it to my local callback so auth.json recovers the same account — workspace, sequences, senders all reappear instantly.

WHEN to call: (a) the user explicitly asks to re-login / says they lost their session, OR (b) a tool call surfaced "Your session has expired or been invalidated by the server" and the current auth.is_anonymous=false (i.e. they HAD a real account before). NEVER call this for a fresh anonymous user who has never claimed — there's no prior account to re-bind to. For anonymous users use growth_claim_account_oauth (creates the account) or growth_claim_account (magic link) instead.

Different from growth_claim_account_oauth: claim is for anon → real conversion (uses linkIdentity, attaches OAuth to current anon user). Re-login is for already-real users who lost their tokens (uses signInWithOAuth, signs into the existing account).

next_path.description: In-app path to land on after re-login completes, e.g. "/w/my-workspace/sequences/seq_abc/builder". Must start with "/". Defaults to "/" if omitted.

switch_account.description: Set true only when the user explicitly wants the MCP to use a different Verbiflow account. This forces the browser OAuth account picker and clears the MCP workspace context after the new account is connected.

tools.name: growth_write_skill_override
tools.description: Persist a user-specific skill override so it applies to every future session. Call this when the user explicitly corrects a behavior ("never do X", "always use Y") OR when you observe the same preference confirmed twice in a session. Overrides are loaded in growth_session_init and patch the skill automatically. Anonymous users cannot save overrides — check auth.is_anonymous before calling.

category.description: Which aspect of the skill this override patches.

rule.description: Plain-English rule to apply. Be specific and actionable, e.g. "Never use contractions in email body copy" or "Default channel_mix to email_only for this user".

confidence.description: "confirmed" = user stated it explicitly. "observed" = inferred from repeated behavior.

tools.name: growth_chrome_run
tools.description:
Drive any site through the user's real Chrome. Opens a tab on `url` if no tab matching the host is already open (no-op when one exists — preserves user state), runs your `js` in it, then returns the post-state HTML and/or markdown plus your script's return value. Use for the long tail of public directories where a typed integration isn't worth it (AICPA peer review, FINRA broker check, NPI registry, state bar listings, FDA Orange Book, EDGAR, etc.).

**Standard scrape loop:** call once with empty `js` (`'return null'`) to get the landing-page HTML → inspect form/table structure → call again with `js` that ticks checkboxes / fills inputs / submits / waits for results → returns post-submit page.

**JS conventions:** wrap in `return` to get a value back. Async OK — `return await fetch(...)` is fine. The return value is JSON-stringified and surfaced in `js_result`. The JS is also where you'd run `await fetch(...)` if you want to hit the site's API directly (cookies, TLS, Cloudflare clearance all ride for free).

**Format param:** `'html'` (default — semantic, has form input names + hidden fields like `__VIEWSTATE`), `'markdown'` (cheaper for the agent to read; loses some semantic info), or `'both'`. Pick markdown when scanning content, html when you need selectors / form names / hidden inputs.

**`incognito: true`** opens the tab in a private window. Use for clean-session anonymous scrapes (no history, no cookies). **Tradeoff:** incognito drops the user's logged-in state, so any auth-walled site fails. Don't combine with sites you need to be signed into.

**Might-get-blocked warning:** if the site uses Cloudflare bot protection, hCaptcha / reCAPTCHA, an interstitial challenge, or sandboxed JS controllers (Pega, Salesforce, ServiceNow, etc.), JS injection may fail or trigger a block. Signs to look for in the response: `html` contains 'Just a moment', 'Access denied', 'cf-browser-verification', '<title>Attention Required'; `js_result` is empty when you expected data; navigation didn't actually fire after `.click()` (the page state didn't change). When that happens, escalate to `growth_chrome_applescript` for OS-level trusted input.

**Prereq (one-time):** Chrome > View > Developer > Allow JavaScript from Apple Events must be ON. The Crunchbase tools auto-flip this; otherwise tell the user to flip the menu item once.

**Same-origin only:** if your `js` does `fetch(otherOrigin)`, browser CORS applies. Open a tab on that origin first.

**Don't poke sensitive tabs uninvited.** If `host_match` could match `mail.google.com`, `slack.com`, `linkedin.com/messaging`, or any site where the agent could send/post/write on the user's behalf — confirm with the user first. Reading public directories needs no confirmation.

url.description: Absolute URL to open if no matching tab exists. Always required. Example: "https://peerreview.aicpa.org/public_file_search.html".

js.description: JavaScript to execute in the tab. Use `return ...` to surface a value via `js_result`. Pass `'return null'` to just snapshot the current page.

host_match.description: URL substring to match an existing tab. Defaults to the URL's host.

format.description: Default `html`. Pick `markdown` for cheap content scans, `html` when you need selectors / form names / hidden inputs, `both` when unsure.

incognito.description: Default false. Set true to open in a private window — clean session, no cookies, no history. Drops the user's logged-in state, so auth-walled sites fail. Use for anonymous public-directory scrapes.

tools.name: growth_chrome_applescript
tools.description:
Run raw AppleScript on the user's Mac. The escape hatch for cases where `growth_chrome_run`'s JS injection isn't enough — most often when a site's controllers gate on `event.isTrusted` and reject synthesized clicks (Pega web mashups, Salesforce Lightning, ServiceNow forms, some Cloudflare challenges). System Events sends real OS-level input that pages can't distinguish from the user.

**When to escalate from `growth_chrome_run` to this tool:**
- `.click()` and `dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click'))` don't trigger the action; UI state doesn't change.
- A page-internal global (Pega's `Grids`, etc.) isn't accessible from injected JS.
- You need to send a keystroke (Tab to focus, Enter to submit, ⌘+L to focus address bar, etc.).
- You need to interact with Chrome's own menus / dialogs (not the page DOM).

**Patterns:**
```applescript
-- Send keystroke to the focused Chrome window
tell application "Google Chrome" to activate
tell application "System Events" to keystroke tab
tell application "System Events" to key code 36  -- Enter

-- Click at screen coordinates (derive via JS first: getBoundingClientRect + window position)
tell application "System Events" to click at {x, y}

-- Run JS in a specific tab AND get the result back
tell application "Google Chrome"
  repeat with t in tabs of window 1
    if URL of t contains "aicpa.org" then
      return execute t javascript "document.querySelector('button.next').click()"
    end if
  end repeat
end tell
```

**Pagination loop pattern (Pega-style sandboxed grid):** focus the page → System Events keystroke Tab repeatedly to land focus on the 'Next' button → key code 36 (Enter) to trigger via real keypress → `growth_chrome_run` to scrape the new state → repeat. Or, derive button screen coordinates via `growth_chrome_run` (read `getBoundingClientRect`, add Chrome window's screen position via `tell application "Google Chrome" to bounds of window 1`), then System Events click at `{x, y}`.

**Returns** `{ stdout, stderr }` — AppleScript's last-expression value lands in stdout. Errors raise.

**Power + responsibility:** AppleScript has full machine access. It can quit apps, click anywhere on screen, send keystrokes to whatever window is focused (including `mail.google.com` if Gmail is up). Don't run scripts that could touch the user's other apps without explicit confirmation.

script.description: Raw AppleScript source. Multi-line OK. Last-expression value goes to stdout. To target Chrome specifically, wrap in `tell application "Google Chrome" ... end tell`. To send OS input, wrap in `tell application "System Events" ... end tell`.

tools.name: growth_chrome_network_log
tools.description:
Monkey-patch a tab's `fetch` + `XMLHttpRequest` to record every request the page makes — useful for reverse-engineering a site's AJAX endpoints. Once you see the actual URL + body the page sends, you can call it directly via `await fetch(...)` inside `growth_chrome_run` and skip pagination clicks entirely.

**Three actions:**
- `'start'` — install the observer in the matching tab. Idempotent (safe to call repeatedly). Optional `filter` substring restricts which requests get logged. Returns `{ js_result: 'started' | 'already_installed' }`.
- `'drain'` — return all entries collected since the last drain (or since start) AND clear the log. Returns `{ entries: [...] }` where each entry is `{ source: 'fetch' | 'xhr', method, url, status, request_body, response_body, started_at, duration_ms }`. Bodies are truncated to `max_body_chars` (default 8000) — bump for larger payloads. Pass `record_headers: true` on `start` to also capture `request_headers` + `response_headers` per entry — handy for reverse-engineering auth/CSRF flows (e.g. LinkedIn Voyager's `x-li-page-instance` + `x-li-track`).
- `'reset'` — clear the log without uninstalling the observer.

**Typical flow:** call `start` with a `filter` (e.g. `"/data/"`, `"api"`) → trigger an action in the page (click Next via `growth_chrome_run` or `growth_chrome_applescript`) → call `drain` to see what the page just fetched. Once you spot the endpoint + body shape, call it directly with `growth_chrome_run` (`await fetch(url, {...})`) — no more clicking.

**Limitation:** the observer survives page navigations within the same origin (no full reload). On a hard reload or a navigation to a different origin, re-call `start`. The patches are non-removable by design (no `stop` action) — they're cheap shims that the page will never notice.

url.description: Tab URL to attach the observer to (opens the tab if no matching tab exists).

action.description: What to do: `start` installs the observer (idempotent), `drain` returns + clears the log, `reset` clears the log without uninstalling.

host_match.description: URL substring to match the tab. Defaults to `url`'s host.

filter.description: Substring filter on request URL. Only requests whose URL contains this substring are logged. Empty string (default) logs everything. Use to cut noise — e.g. `"/data/"`, `"graphql"`, `"api.example.com"`.

max_body_chars.description: Max chars per request_body / response_body in the log. Default 8000. Bump if you need to capture larger payloads.

record_headers.description: Default false. When true, each entry also includes `request_headers` and `response_headers`. Set when reverse-engineering auth/CSRF flows.

tools.name: growth_list_clay_tables
tools.description: List Clay tables + workbooks the user has access to, using their local browser Clay session. macOS only. Workspace auto-discovered from the cookie unless `workspace_id` is pinned. Pass `query` to search by name (e.g. "fintech") — server-side filter, narrow + fast. Without `query`: returns up to 30 most-recently-opened tables. With `query`: returns ALL matches (no cap). Returns { tables: [{table_id, view_id, name, workbook_id, workbook_name, row_type, last_opened_at, workspace_id, workspace_name}, ...] }. `view_id` is often null in the list response — `growth_import_clay_table` resolves it lazily at import time. On mode: "unsupported", the user has no Clay session in that browser — ask them to log into Clay there, or try the other browser.

browser.description: Which browser the user is logged into Clay on.

query.description: Optional name filter. When set, server-side searches across ALL workbooks + tables in scope (uses isGlobalSearch). When omitted, returns the most-recently-opened items only.

workspace_id.description: OPTIONAL. Usually omit — workspaces are auto-discovered from the cookie. Pass only if the user explicitly names a specific workspace id.

tools.name: growth_import_clay_table
tools.description: Export a specific Clay table as CSV using the user's local Clay session, then upload it to the named source node on a sequence draft (creates a staging session — same path the web CSV-upload flow uses). Use after growth_list_clay_tables / growth_parse_clay_table_url has identified the table_id + view_id the user picked. Requires an existing sequence draft with a source node (get source_node_id from growth_get_sequence). Returns { source_run_id, row_count, columns }. For arbitrary customer Clay tables, pass column_mapping when the columns are custom or ambiguous so staging/enrichment can use trusted canonical fields immediately. Surface the row_count to the user. macOS only (Clay cookie read).

browser.description: Which browser the user is logged into Clay on.

source_node_id.description: The source node id on the sequence draft to attach this CSV to.

ingress_id.description: Optional ingress id if the source node has multiple ingresses.

column_mapping.description: Optional explicit canonical mapping for customer-owned Clay tables. Use when the Clay table is arbitrary or has custom headers. Shape: {"contact_email":"Email","contact_linkedin_url":"LinkedIn Profile","company_domain":"Website"}. If omitted, only recognized aliases are mapped immediately and backend dynamic mapping may resolve the rest asynchronously.

tools.name: growth_parse_clay_table_url
tools.description: Parse a Clay table URL (the one the user sees in their browser tab when viewing a table) into its workspace_id / workbook_id / table_id / view_id components. Use this when the workspace has too many tables for growth_list_clay_tables to be useful, OR when the user just wants to use a specific table and has pasted its URL. Does NOT need the browser cookie — pure URL parsing.

tools.name: growth_search_clay_people
tools.description:
Run a Clay People Search using the user's own Clay account (browser session cookies). 

*** WHAT THIS IS: a PERSONA search — finds people who CURRENTLY hold a given title at companies matching firmographics (size / industry / location). Examples: "VPs of Servicing at mortgage companies 51-500 in the US", "DONs at hospice agencies", "Founders at YC W24 cos". 

*** WHAT THIS IS NOT: a HIRING SIGNAL search. If the user's play is "target companies actively hiring for {role}" (job_posting play, hiring-pain trigger), DO NOT use this tool — there is no live-job predicate here, just current title. Use the native `job_posting` audience source (Flage built-in, cleanest), or growth_search_clay_jobs to pull companies with live posts then chain into growth_find_people_at_companies for the right contacts. Confusing persona-search with hiring-signal is a recurring failure mode — read this carefully before picking. 

ASYNC. This call returns within seconds with `{ job_id, status: "running" }`. Clay searches take 4-8 min at typical scale (most of that is Clay streaming rows into the table — not anything we control). The actual work happens in the background; you MUST poll growth_clay_search_status({job_id}) every 15-30s to see progress and get the final CSV. Polling returns `current_rows` while streaming, then `result.csv_path` + sample + columns when complete. 

TWO MODES based on whether a sequence draft is passed: 

• DISCOVERY mode (no sequence_id + source_node_id) — pure search. When complete, status payload contains: { csv_path, sample, row_count, columns, company_domains, table_id, view_id, workbook_id }. Use when the user just wants to see the people (e.g. before committing to an audience, or when joining multiple searches). 

• ATTACH mode (both sequence_id AND source_node_id passed) — runs the search AND stages + promotes the rows as the sequence's audience. When complete, status payload also includes { source_run_id, promote_status, lead_list_id }. Requires an existing sequence draft. 

*** ALWAYS pass `filters.limit_per_company` (default: 5–10). Clay returns every contact that matches your filters — without a per- company cap, a single large company (e.g. JPMorgan in a financial- services search) floods the audience with dozens of contacts and crowds out the smaller companies that matter for the play. 5 for tight personas, 10 for broader ones. There is no global `limit` knob (intentionally — capping the total truncates the audience and hides whether filters are too narrow). 

Both modes save the CSV to $TMPDIR/flage-clay/ and register it in the manifest (growth_clay_list_saved_results). macOS only (Clay cookie read). If the user has multiple Clay workspaces, pass workspace_id explicitly.

sequence_id.description: Optional. Pass to ATTACH mode (stages + promotes rows as the sequence audience). Omit for DISCOVERY mode (pure search). If set, source_node_id is also required.

source_node_id.description: Optional. Required only if sequence_id is passed. Identifies which source node on the sequence draft to land the CSV on.

workspace_id.description: Clay workspace id. Optional — when omitted, auto-discovered from the cookie; errors if the user has more than one workspace.

workbook_name.description: Name for the NEW Clay workbook to create. Ignored if workbook_id is set.

workbook_id.description: Existing Clay workbook id (starts with wb_). When set, the new people table is created inside that workbook instead of creating a new one. Get workbook_id from growth_list_clay_tables — it's on every returned row.

table_name.description: Optional label for the table that gets created. Defaults to "Find people".

filters.description: Clay people-search filters. At least one must be non-empty (e.g. job_title_keywords, company_identifier, location_countries_include). See backend/flage/bridge/clay/payload.py for the full set.

job_title_seniority_levels.description: Allowed: intern, junior, associate, mid, senior, lead, manager, director, vp, cxo, founder, owner, partner, principal, staff.

job_functions.description: Allowed: engineering, product, design, marketing, sales, success, support, finance, hr, ops, legal, security, it, data, executive, growth, business.

company_identifier.description: Domains (or Clay-accepted company IDs) to seed the search from. Combine with start_from_method="CsvOfCompanies" to search people at specific companies.

company_industries_include.description: Exact Clay industry names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="industries") to get valid values.

company_industries_exclude.description: Exact Clay industry names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="industries") to get valid values.

location_countries_include.description: Exact country names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="countries") to get valid values.

headline_keywords.description: Substring match on the LinkedIn headline (the one-liner under the name). Combine with about_keywords and/or job_title_keywords to narrow further — e.g. job_title_keywords=["recruiter"] + headline_keywords=["hardware"] for hardware recruiters. AND-ed with the other filters; values within the array are OR-ed.

about_keywords.description: Substring match on the LinkedIn About section (long bio). Combine with headline_keywords and/or job_title_keywords to narrow — e.g. about_keywords=["hardware"] + headline_keywords=["hardware"] catches anyone who self-describes as hardware-focused. AND-ed with the other filters; values within the array are OR-ed.

profile_keywords.description: Substring match across the full LinkedIn profile text (broader than about/headline). Use when you want any mention anywhere in the profile, not just headline or bio.

limit_per_company.description: Cap on how many people Clay returns per company. DEFAULT: pass 5–10 (5 for tight personas, 10 for broader). Without this, one large company floods the result set and crowds out the smaller companies that matter for the play. This is the diversification knob — pass it on every call. (Note: there is no global `limit` knob — Clay returns every contact that matches the filters.)

tools.name: growth_clay_search_status
tools.description:
Poll the status of a Clay search started via growth_search_clay_people, growth_search_clay_companies, or growth_search_clay_jobs. All three are async and return a `job_id`. Pass that `job_id` here. Returns: 
- `status`: "running" | "complete" | "failed" | "unknown" 
- `message`: short human-readable summary of the current step 
- `current_rows`: rows materialized in Clay so far (during streaming) 
- `log`: last ~40 progress lines with elapsed timestamps 
- `result`: populated when status="complete" — includes `csv_path`, `row_count`, `sample`, `columns`, `company_domains`, `table_id`, `view_id`, etc. For attach mode, also includes `source_run_id`, `promote_status`, `lead_list_id`. 
- `error`: populated when status="failed" 

Cadence: poll every 15-30 seconds while running. A typical search (10-50k rows) takes 4-8 min — most of which is Clay streaming rows. The fastest you can get the CSV is bound by Clay's upstream search throughput, not by polling frequency. Don't poll faster than every 10s — it adds load with no benefit. 

If status="unknown", the job_id never existed or its state was cleaned up (>7 days old). State persists across MCP-server restarts.

job_id.description: The job_id returned by growth_search_clay_people, growth_search_clay_companies, or growth_search_clay_jobs.

tools.name: growth_clay_export_csv
tools.description:
Export an EXISTING Clay table to a CSV on the local filesystem. No sequence required — the CSV path is returned for the model to read or pass into other tools (growth_join_clay_results_by_domain, growth_upload_clay_csv_to_sequence, etc.). 

Pass exactly ONE of the identifier args: 
- `table_id` (+ optional `view_id`; defaults to the table's firstViewId) 
- `table_url` (full Clay app URL — parsed for ids) 
- `job_id` (a previously-completed growth_search_clay_people job — the underlying table_id + view_id are read from the job state file) 
- `table_name` (substring; only works if exactly one table matches in the user's workspace — otherwise this errors with the candidates so the model can disambiguate) 

When to use this vs the other tools: 
- growth_search_clay_people / _companies / _jobs already write a CSV AND return its path — call this AFTER the fact only if you discarded the csv_path or the search completed in a previous conversation. 
- growth_import_clay_table attaches the CSV to a sequence audience — use that when the user wants the data in a sequence draft, not on disk. 

Returns the same shape as discovery-mode search: { csv_path, row_count, columns, sample, company_domains, table_id, view_id, workbook_id }. Typical runtime: 30-90s depending on row count (export + S3 download).

table_id.description: Clay table id (starts with t_). Pair with view_id for a non-default view.

view_id.description: Clay view id (starts with gv_). Optional — defaults to the table's firstViewId.

job_id.description: A previously-completed Clay search job id (clay_people_...). The table_id + view_id are read from the job's state file.

table_name.description: Substring match on table name. Resolved server-side; errors with candidates if more than one table matches.

tools.name: growth_search_clay_companies
tools.description:
Run a Clay Company Search (find-lists-of-companies) using the user's own Clay account (browser session cookies). DISCOVERY tool — does NOT stage rows to a sequence. 

ASYNC: returns a `job_id` immediately and runs the search in the background; you MUST poll growth_clay_search_status({job_id}) every 15-30s. When status="complete", the `result` field carries { csv_path, sample, company_domains, table_id, view_id, workbook_id, columns, row_count }. Feed company_domains into growth_search_clay_people's company_identifier[] to find contacts at these companies. 

BEST PRACTICE — semantic_description is the strongest single lever. Treat it like a concept prompt, not a keyword. When the user says "lead enrichment tools" or "find companies like Clearbit", DO NOT pass "lead enrichment" verbatim. Expand it into a rich 1-3 sentence description of what those companies actually do: what they sell, who they sell to, what their product category is called. Example: "B2B SaaS that enriches contact and company records with firmographic, technographic, and behavioral data. Typically sold to sales / marketing teams for prospecting and ABM. Comparable companies: Clearbit, ZoomInfo, Apollo, People Data Labs, Cognism." Clay's ranking is embedding-based — more specific concept text = better look-alikes. 

Combine semantic_description with structural filters (sizes, country_names, technographics_vendors, minimum_member_count) to narrow. locations / locations_exclude accept free-form strings (cities, states, regions) and DO NOT require a search_raw_location flag — that flag is people-search only. macOS only (cookie read).

workspace_id.description: Clay workspace id. Optional — auto-discovered when omitted.

workbook_name.description: Name for the NEW Clay workbook to create. Ignored if workbook_id is set.

workbook_id.description: Existing Clay workbook id (starts with wb_). When set, the new company table is created inside that workbook instead of creating a new one. Useful for chaining multiple searches (company + jobs + people) into the same workbook.

table_name.description: Optional label for the table. Defaults to "Find companies".

filters.description: Clay company-search filters. At least one must be non-empty. Common: semantic_description (free-text concept like "chip design"), industries[], country_names[], locations[] (free-form), sizes[], annual_revenues[], technographics_vendors[], minimum_member_count.

semantic_description.description: Free-text concept / theme — e.g. "chip design", "B2B SaaS payroll", "generative AI for legal".

industries.description: Exact Clay industry names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="industries") to get valid values.

industries_exclude.description: Exact Clay industry names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="industries") to get valid values.

country_names.description: Exact country names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="countries") to get valid values.

country_names_exclude.description: Exact country names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="countries") to get valid values.

company_identifier.description: Optional seed domains. Empty + semantic_description = search all companies matching the concept.

tools.name: growth_search_clay_jobs
tools.description:
Run a Clay Job-Posting Search (find-lists-of-jobs) using the user's own Clay account. DISCOVERY tool — does NOT stage rows to a sequence. 

ASYNC: returns a `job_id` immediately and runs the search in the background; you MUST poll growth_clay_search_status({job_id}) every 15-30s. When status="complete", the `result` field carries { csv_path, sample, row_count, columns, company_domains, table_id, workbook_id }. Typical use: find companies actively hiring for a role → pipe company_domains into growth_search_clay_people (with a job_title_keywords filter matching the persona) to reach the people doing that role at the hiring companies. 

USE THESE FILTERS (Clay's jobs output is reliable on them):
  - job_title_keywords — the primary signal. Substring match.
  - job_description_keywords — matches text in the posting body.
  - locations — free-form strings. Country (e.g. "United States"), state, metro, or city — Clay fuzzy-matches. Multiple values OR together.
  - min_num_days_since_posted / max_num_days_since_posted — recency window. Use max=30 for "posted in the last month".

AVOID THESE FILTERS (Clay's job data on these is noisy / inconsistent — results drop too aggressively):
  - employment_type (full-time/contract/etc.) — missing / mislabeled on many postings.
  - seniority — Clay infers this heuristically from the title and often gets it wrong. Rely on job_title_keywords instead (e.g. `["senior", "staff"]` or `["vp", "head of"]`).

There is no `limit` knob (intentionally — capping the count would truncate the audience and hide whether the filters are too narrow). Clay returns every matching job posting.

macOS only.

filters.description: Clay job-posting-search filters. At least one must be non-empty. Common: job_title_keywords, seniority, employment_type, min/max_num_days_since_posted, locations, company_identifier (seed list).

seniority.description: Free-form strings, lowercased. Clay silently drops unknown values.

company_identifier.description: Optional seed company domains to scope the search to.

tools.name: growth_join_clay_results_by_domain
tools.description: Join CSVs from a company search, people search, and/or jobs search on the canonical company_domain key (lowercased, www-stripped, path-stripped). Reads the csv_path returned by each growth_search_clay_* call, joins row-by-row on normalized company_domain, writes a merged summary CSV (one row per domain with aggregated people/jobs counts + first-N samples) and a detail JSON file (full nested structure), and returns { csv_path, json_path, row_count, sample, counts }. Use after running 2+ of the growth_search_clay_* tools to see which companies appear across multiple searches (e.g. "which chip-design companies are ALSO hiring security guards?"). Pure client-side — no Clay API calls, no extra credits.

companies_csv_path.description: Path returned in the `csv_path` field of a prior growth_search_clay_companies call. Typically /tmp/flage-clay/company-t_xxx-<ts>.csv.

people_csv_path.description: Path returned in the `csv_path` field of a prior growth_search_clay_people call (people search also writes its CSV to tmp alongside the staged audience).

jobs_csv_path.description: Path returned in the `csv_path` field of a prior growth_search_clay_jobs call.

tools.name: growth_clay_list_saved_results
tools.description: List every Clay CSV / JSON saved locally in this session by growth_search_clay_* and growth_join_clay_results_by_domain. Returns a manifest of { path, kind, entity_kind, label, row_count, table_id, workbook_id, saved_at } so the LLM can recall what's on disk without re-running searches. Use when the user asks "what do I have so far?" or when building a join and needing to find the paths of earlier search results. Pure filesystem read — no Clay or backend calls.

kind.description: Filter to a single kind. Omit to return all saved artifacts.

entity_kind.description: Filter to a single entity kind. Omit to return all.

tools.name: growth_upload_csv_to_sequence
tools.description:
Stage a CSV file (from ANY source — Clay searches, the join output, a user-provided path, etc.) onto a sequence draft as its audience. Reads csv_path from disk, validates the headers, then runs the same staging + promotion path used by growth_import_clay_table and the web CSV-upload flow. Returns { source_run_id, row_count, columns, promote_status, lead_list_id, column_mapping }. 

VALIDATION — this tool REQUIRES the CSV to have at least one contact identifier column: an email column (email, email_address) OR a LinkedIn URL column (linkedin_url, linkedin_profile, profile_url, etc.). Without one of those, Flage has no way to reach the contacts. The LLM should verify this BEFORE calling the tool — inspect the `columns` field returned by the search tool (or read the CSV header with a file tool) and confirm the user's CSV has email or linkedin_url. If it doesn't, surface the issue instead of calling this — company-only or job-posting CSVs cannot be staged as an audience; they need to be chained through a people search first. 

Use after growth_search_clay_people (discovery mode), growth_join_clay_results_by_domain (if the join CSV has contact columns), or any user-provided CSV on disk. NOT needed when growth_search_clay_people is called in ATTACH mode (sequence_id + source_node_id passed) — that path already stages.

csv_path.description: Absolute path to the CSV to upload. Typically the csv_path from a prior growth_search_clay_* / growth_join_clay_results_by_domain call, but can be any CSV the user points at.

source_node_id.description: Source node on the sequence draft to attach the CSV to.

ingress_id.description: Optional ingress id if the source node has multiple ingresses.

list_label.description: Human-readable label shown on the lead list in the builder UI. Defaults to "CSV · {filename}".

file_label.description: Filename label used by the staging endpoint. Defaults to the CSV's basename (without .csv suffix).

column_mapping.description: Explicit target mapping for generic/user CSVs when headers are not already canonical or recognized aliases. Shape: {"contact_email":"Email Address","contact_linkedin_url":"LinkedIn","company_domain":"Website"}. Values may also be full objects: {"contact_email":{"source_column_name":"Email Address","category":"contact_identifier","label":"Email"}}. Accepted categories are contact_identifier, company_identifier, contact_enrichment, company_enrichment. Use canonical target keys such as contact_email, contact_linkedin_url, contact_full_name, contact_first_name, contact_last_name, contact_job_title, company_name, company_domain, company_website, company_linkedin_url, company_description. Unmapped raw columns remain source_row/display data and are not promoted as resolver-trusted enrichment fields. Agents should pass this for non-Clay/user CSVs with custom headers instead of relying on raw header names.

tools.name: growth_check_csv_variable_coverage
tools.description:
Check whether a CSV has values for the template variables ({{first_name}}, {{company_name}}, etc.) used in a sequence's message copy. Call this BEFORE growth_upload_csv_to_sequence so you can warn the user (or pick a different CSV / enrich first) when too many leads are missing fields. 

Pass `variables` as the list extracted from the copy — strip the curly braces, e.g. ["first_name", "company_name", "job_title"]. Returns { total_leads, per_variable_coverage, leads_with_missing, all_have_required, summary }. `per_variable_coverage` gives missing_count + missing_percent per variable; `leads_with_missing` lists row indices + identifier + the variables they lack so you can show the user concrete examples.

csv_path.description: Absolute path to the CSV to check.

variables.description: List of template variable names (without {{}}) used in the sequence copy. Inspect the message body / subject / connection note / linkedin message and pull every {{var}}. Sender variables (sender_name, sender_first_name, sender_email, sender_title) are ignored — they come from the sender.

column_mapping.description: Optional explicit mapping from canonical field key → CSV column header, same shape as growth_upload_csv_to_sequence.column_mapping. Use when CSV headers are ambiguous.

sample_size.description: Cap on how many bad-lead examples to return in leads_with_missing (default 20). Coverage stats always cover the full CSV.

tools.name: growth_get_clay_enums
tools.description: Look up valid Clay filter values for a given field. Use this before constructing search filters to get exact string values that Clay accepts. Supports optional keyword search to narrow a large list (e.g. search "software" in industries). Returns the field type, which tools/filters it applies to, total count, and the matching values. Fields: "industries" (applies to company + people industry filters), "countries" (applies to country_names and location_countries_include).

field.description: Which enum field to look up.

search.description: Optional keyword to filter the list (case-insensitive substring match). Omit to get all values.

tools.name: growth_join_csv_files
tools.description:
Join two CSV files on a shared column and write the merged result to disk. Pure local operation — no network, no browser session. Default is a LEFT JOIN: every row from the left CSV is kept; matching columns from the right CSV are appended. Use this whenever you have two CSVs about the same entities (e.g. a people CSV with company_linkedin_url + a companies CSV with company_linkedin_url + company_domain + company_name) and you want a single CSV with all the columns. 

Pass `on` when both sides share the same column name; pass `left_on` + `right_on` when the names differ. `normalize_key` handles common normalization gotchas: "linkedin_url" strips /about/, trailing slashes, query strings, and lowercases; "domain" strips https://, www., paths; "lowercase" just lowercases; "none" matches as-is. 

Returns { csv_path, matched_rows, unmatched_left, unmatched_right, columns } so you can immediately see how clean the join was.

left_csv_path.description: Absolute path to the LEFT CSV (the side whose rows are kept under the default left-join). Typically the larger / row-level file (e.g. people).

right_csv_path.description: Absolute path to the RIGHT CSV (the side providing extra columns to merge in). Typically the smaller / lookup-style file (e.g. companies).

on.description: Join column name (must exist on both sides). Use this OR `left_on`+`right_on`.

left_on.description: Join column name on the LEFT CSV. Only needed when column names differ.

right_on.description: Join column name on the RIGHT CSV. Only needed when column names differ.

how.description: Default "left". inner = drop unmatched on both sides. left = keep all left rows. right = keep all right rows. outer = keep everything.

normalize_key.description: How to normalize the join key before matching. Default "lowercase". Use "linkedin_url" for company LinkedIn URLs (strips /about/, trailing slashes, query strings), "domain" for hostnames (strips https://, www., paths).

output_label.description: Optional label for the output filename. Default "joined".

tools.name: growth_get_data_source_options
tools.description: Returns the available data source options for a given play, filtered by which tools the user has connected. Call this immediately after the user confirms the play + channel_mix, BEFORE any search. If needs_user_choice is true, show the options and ask the user to pick. If false, proceed silently with the single option returned. Always surface CSV upload as an additional fallback regardless of the result.

play.description: The play kind the user confirmed. Use one of: "hiring_signal", "persona_search", "post_reactors", "incubator", "recently_funded", "same_investor_portfolio", "company_search". Pass the closest match — the tool returns an empty options list for unknown plays.

connected_tools.description: Tool names the user has connected (from growth_session_init connected_tools where present=true). E.g. ["clay", "crunchbase"]. Pass an empty array if none are connected.

tools.name: growth_research_company
tools.description: Deeply research a company by domain — scrapes their homepage for hero copy / customer logos / testimonials, resolves their LinkedIn company page, finds founders, and pulls the last 5 posts from each founder + the company page. Cached 30 days per domain. Blocks up to ~45s for a fresh run; if it's still not done, returns status "running" with a workflow_id so the skill can tell the user to hold on. ALWAYS confirm with the user before calling this tool (never mention cost/credits/quotas to the user — onboarding is free for them).

force.description: Re-run even if a fresh cached result exists. Default false.

wait_seconds.description: How long to poll before returning a running status. Default 45.

tools.name: growth_get_company_research
tools.description: Return the latest stored company-research payload for a domain, without waiting. Use when the user returns after a long gap and you want to check whether a previously-kicked-off workflow has completed since.

tools.name: growth_find_investor_portfolio
tools.description: Given a VC firm name (e.g. "Sequoia Capital", "Andreessen Horowitz", "Y Combinator"), return the list of companies they've publicly invested in by scraping the firm's own portfolio page. Used by the "same-investor warm intro" play (see ~/.claude/skills/growth/playbook.md) to build a target list of other companies backed by the user's own investors. Cached 90 days per investor. Confirm with the user before calling (never mention cost/credits — onboarding is free for them).

investor_name.description: The VC firm name. Can be the short form ("a16z", "YC") or the full name ("Andreessen Horowitz", "Y Combinator").

tools.name: growth_enrich_companies
tools.description:
Bulk-enrich a list of LinkedIn company URLs with firmographic data (name, employee count, industry, HQ, founded year, description). Lightweight wrapper around the company-enrichment pipeline — pick the exact fields you want from the enrichments enum, and the response only contains those fields. Up to 25 URLs per call; sync, completes in 30-90s for typical batches.

INPUT IS LINKEDIN URLS ONLY. If you have domains, call growth_resolve_company_linkedin_urls first to convert them.

Common use: confirming target company size before locking an audience (e.g. "the Clay job search returned Google + Uber alongside real targets — pull employee_count_band on the top 25 to see how many are sub-150-emp"). NEVER auto-filter by size silently — surface the result to the user and let them decide whether the big-co names belong.

linkedin_urls.description: LinkedIn company / school URLs (e.g. "https://linkedin.com/company/anthropic"). Pass plain URLs — the backend normalizes /about and trailing slashes.

enrichments.description: Exact fields to return per company. `employee_count_band` is the LinkedIn size string ("11-50 employees", "1,001-5,000 employees", etc.) — best for size-band smell tests. `employee_count` is the numeric value when available. `industries` is an array. `headquarters` is a free-form string (e.g. "San Francisco, California"). Keep the list short — unrequested fields are dropped, no over-fetch.

tools.name: growth_reconcile_billing
tools.description: Force the user's workspace subscription to re-sync its per-product quantities (email mailboxes, LinkedIn accounts, etc.) against the actual count of connected senders. Call this AFTER the user confirms a Stripe checkout completed, so seats created via MCP pre-payment get billed on the fresh subscription. Also safe to call any time the user reports a billing mismatch ("I connected LinkedIn but it's not on my invoice"). Idempotent and fast — no-op on orgs with no subscription.

tools.name: growth_connect_linkedin_from_cookies
tools.description: Create a real, persistent LinkedIn sender in the user's workspace by reading the user's active LinkedIn session from their local browser. REQUIRES the `browser` arg: "chrome" or "safari" — ask the user which browser they're logged into LinkedIn on before calling this. In gateway mode the configured GROWTH_MCP_BROWSER_PROVIDER is used instead so the cookie read stays inside the scoped gateway browser identity. No extension, no platform visit. The backend connects the account through Unipile and derives the display name + profile URL from the account metadata. Use this when growth_list_senders shows has_linkedin_account === false AND the user has consented to pulling their local LinkedIn session. macOS/Windows only — returns { mode: "unsupported" } elsewhere; skill should fall back to the senders_url flow. Safari extraction requires Claude Code to have Full Disk Access (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access); if the user picks Safari and the call fails with a permissions error, instruct them to grant FDA + restart Claude Code, then retry.

browser.description: Which browser the user is currently logged into LinkedIn on. Required on macOS. Windows only supports "chrome".

chrome_profile.description: Optional Chrome profile name when browser="chrome" (default: "Default").

sender_id.description: Optional. When set, the LinkedIn account is attached to this existing sender instead of creating a new one — use this whenever growth_list_senders returned a sender for this user, so they don't end up with duplicate sender rows (one for email, one for LinkedIn). Omit only for a truly fresh workspace where the LinkedIn connect is the first sender creation.

tools.name: growth_create_sender
tools.description: Create a new sender (the identity that does the sending) in the user's workspace. Call this ONLY when growth_list_senders returned an empty array AND the user has given you their first name, last name, and (optionally) email. This is the FIRST step of onboarding a net-new user — it makes a sender row they can then attach a mailbox or LinkedIn account to. After this returns, immediately follow up with one of: growth_connect_linkedin_from_cookies, growth_connect_mailbox_oauth, or growth_connect_mailbox_app_password — do NOT leave the user with a sender that has no channel connected. Returns { sender_id, display_name, primary_email, ... }.

primary_email.description: The sender's primary email address. Optional but strongly recommended — pass it whenever the user has given it; it's used for display + as a default identifier when connecting a mailbox.

display_name.description: Optional display override. When omitted, the backend derives it from first + last name.

tools.name: growth_move_sender_account
tools.description: Move a single sender_account (mailbox or LinkedIn) from one sender to another within the same workspace. The canonical use-case: merge two duplicate senders for the same human — e.g. the email connect created one sender and an earlier LinkedIn connect created a second — by moving the account from the duplicate onto the primary sender, then deleting the now-empty duplicate. Reversible: call again with the original sender_id to move it back. Doesn't recreate anything, just repoints `sender_accounts.sender_id`. Call growth_list_senders first to pick the `sender_account_id` of the account to move and the `target_sender_id` of the sender to move it onto.

sender_account_id.description: The sender_account_id to move (from growth_list_senders → senders[].accounts[].sender_account_id).

target_sender_id.description: The sender_id to move the account onto (from growth_list_senders → senders[].sender_id).

tools.name: growth_get_mailbox_oauth_quote
tools.description: Quote the cost of the next Gmail / Microsoft OAuth mailbox connect for this workspace. Call this RIGHT BEFORE asking the user 'OAuth or app password?" so you can tell them how many free OAuth mailboxes they have left vs. how much the next one will cost. Returns { current_count, free_quota, will_be_charged, price_cents, requires_workspace_subscription, has_workspace_subscription }. Rule of thumb wording: if `will_be_charged === false` → *"OAuth: free, you've used {current_count} of {free_quota} free mailboxes."*. If `will_be_charged === true` → *"OAuth: the next mailbox is ${price_cents/100}/mo (you've already used your {free_quota} free ones)."*. App password is always free regardless — mention that in the same breath so the user can make an informed pick.

tools.name: growth_connect_mailbox_oauth
tools.description: Generate a Unipile hosted-OAuth link the user clicks to connect a Gmail or Microsoft mailbox to an existing sender. Returns { auth_url, provider_link_id, will_be_charged, price_cents }. Send the `auth_url` back to the user verbatim — they open it, authorize in the provider's own UI, and Unipile's webhook creates the sender_account row. Use this when the user wants to connect an email mailbox and has a standard Gmail/Microsoft account (NOT when they're stuck with an IMAP-only / custom-domain account — those need growth_connect_mailbox_app_password). Requires a sender — call growth_create_sender first if growth_list_senders was empty.

sender_id.description: ID of the sender to attach the mailbox to. From growth_list_senders / growth_create_sender.

tools.name: growth_connect_mailbox_app_password
tools.description: Connect a Gmail mailbox via an IMAP/SMTP app password — the fallback when OAuth won't work (Workspace admin disabled it, custom domain routed through Gmail, etc.). Two steps under the hood (auth/start + provider-links complete); chained here so the agent makes one call. The user must have already generated an app password at https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords (requires 2-step verification enabled). Returns { sender_account_id, identifier, ... } on success. On invalid-password errors, surface the backend message verbatim — it's the user's cue to regenerate the app password and retry.

sender_id.description: ID of the sender to attach the mailbox to. From growth_list_senders / growth_create_sender.

email.description: The Gmail address being connected. Used as the IMAP/SMTP identifier.

app_password.description: The 16-character app password from https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords. Spaces are stripped server-side. Never log this.

tools.name: growth_connect_crunchbase
tools.description: Verify the user is signed into Crunchbase in Chrome. Auto-configures the "Allow JavaScript from Apple Events" Chrome policy if it's off (writes the policy via `defaults` + restarts Chrome so it takes effect), opens a crunchbase.com tab if none exists, then calls /v4/cb/sessions to confirm the connected account. On first run the user may briefly see Chrome quit and relaunch — tabs are restored.

open_if_missing.description: Default true. If no crunchbase.com tab is open, open one automatically.

auto_fix_chrome.description: Default true. If the "Allow JavaScript from Apple Events" Chrome policy is off, write the policy + restart Chrome automatically. Set false to get a diagnostic instead.

tools.name: growth_resolve_crunchbase_entities
tools.description: Translate human names into Crunchbase UUIDs via /v4/data/autocompletes. Works for industries (collection="categories"), broader category groups ("category_groups"), investors ("principal.investors"), companies ("organization.companies"), or locations ("locations"). Returns matched / unmatched / ambiguous buckets. Use when the user names an entity and you need its UUID for a search predicate.

tools.name: growth_search_crunchbase_companies
tools.description: Search Crunchbase for companies matching firmographic filters (industries, category groups, employee size, last-funding date/type/amount, investors). Human names for industries/investors are resolved automatically via autocomplete. Returns a CSV path + sample + next_cursor for pagination. Default `pages: -1` walks all matching pages up to the recommended cap of 20 (= 1000 rows at default `limit: 50`); pass an explicit `pages: N` (max 100) to override the recommended cap when the user has confirmed a bigger pull. Sleeps `sleep_ms` ± 33% jitter between pages (default 1500ms). Stops early when Crunchbase returns no next_cursor; partial results are returned if a mid-loop page errors. To go beyond the recommended cap, either resume with `after_id` or pass an explicit `pages: N`. For a cheap discovery call (just to read `total_matching` before deciding how much to pull), pass `pages: 1`.

industries.description: Human category names (e.g. "FinTech"). Resolved via autocomplete.

industry_uuids.description: Pre-resolved category UUIDs. Mixed with `industries` via set union.

category_groups.description: Human broader-industry names (e.g. "Software"). Resolved via autocomplete.

last_funding_types.description: Funding stages (seed, series_a, series_b, pre_seed, debt_financing, ...).

investors.description: Human investor names (e.g. "Andreessen Horowitz"). Resolved via autocomplete.

keyword.description: Local substring filter over name + description (Crunchbase advanced search has no free-text predicate).

after_id.description: Pagination cursor for the FIRST page. Pass a previous call's next_cursor to resume. With `pages` > 1 the loop continues from here.

pages.description: How many pages to fetch in one call. Default -1 (= fetch all matching, capped at the recommended 20 pages = 1000 rows at default `limit`). Pass an explicit `pages: N` to override the recommended cap (absolute max 100) — only after the user confirms they want a bigger pull. Loop stops early when Crunchbase returns no next_cursor; sets stop_reason="hard_cap" when a cap was the stopper. Pass `pages: 1` for a cheap discovery call.

sleep_ms.description: Base sleep between pages when fetching > 1 page. Actual delay is randomized ±33% around this value. Default 1500ms (effective range 1000–2000ms — looks human-paced, stays clear of Cloudflare). Max 10000ms.

tools.name: growth_deanonymize_contacts
tools.description: Start an async workflow to deanonymize a batch of partial contact records into LinkedIn profiles. For each contact, pass any 2+ of {first_name, last_name, company_name, company_domain, job_title, location}. Internally runs a LinkedIn people-search with first/last name + company (preferred) or job_title (fallback when no company is known); location is intentionally not used as a filter. If `company_domain` is supplied it is resolved to the LinkedIn company URL directly (exact lookup); otherwise `company_name` is resolved via search. If the primary search returns 0 hits, a hailmary retry drops the disambiguator and re-queries with just the name. The LLM picker then chooses the best candidate from up to 3, but `candidates` always carries the full list so the agent can override. Returns {job_id} immediately — poll growth_get_deanonymize_contacts_results to read the resolved profiles. Per-record results cached 14d. Default confidence gate is 60. Hard cap: 50 contacts per call. Never reveal the underlying vendor / actor details to the user; describe behavior only.

company_domain.description: Company website domain (e.g. "recall.ai"). When provided, used to resolve the LinkedIn company URL directly instead of guessing from `company_name`. If both are passed, `company_domain` wins.

location.description: Captured for context but NOT used as a search filter — location strings rarely match the LinkedIn-side normalization and tend to zero out otherwise-good searches.

contacts.description: Array of partial contact records. Each record MUST have at least 2 non-empty fields. Empty strings are dropped before counting.

confidence_threshold.description: Minimum confidence (0-100) for `found: true`. Default 60. Below this, the best candidate is still returned in `profile` for context but `found` is false with reason "low_confidence".

skip_cache.description: If true, bypass the 14-day S3 cache and run a fresh lookup. Default false.

tools.name: growth_get_deanonymize_contacts_results
tools.description: Fetch status + results from a deanonymize-contacts job. `finished: false` means the workflow is still running — poll again in a few seconds. `finished: true` and `failed: false` means `results` is the final list (one entry per input contact). Each result has flat top-level fields {found, confidence, linkedin_url, title, full_name, first_name, last_name, company_name, location, reason} pulled out of the LinkedIn search payload — use these directly when building a CSV instead of digging into `profile`. The raw `profile` object is also returned for any field not flattened, and `candidates` carries every profile the search returned (up to 3 from Apify + Serper /in fallback) so you can override the LLM pick if it looks wrong. Title prefers structured currentPosition[0].position over the (often decorated) headline. `failed: true` surfaces `error_message`. `summary` (total/found/not_found/cached/hit_rate) is included only when finished successfully. Results are NOT paginated — the whole batch (≤50) is returned in one call.

tools.name: growth_get_external_tools_used
tools.description: Silently detect which third-party sales tools the user is logged into by checking local browser cookie existence (no decryption, no password prompts, no network calls). Call this in the session-start detection burst — the result GATES which discovery tools are allowed in play-proposal alternatives. macOS only. Currently probes: Clay (chrome / safari), Crunchbase (chrome only). Returns { tools: [{name, present, browser, integrated}, ...] } where `browser` is "chrome" | "safari" | null, and `integrated` is true if we have an actual data-pull integration for that tool today (vs. acknowledgment-only). NEVER surface a tool whose `present` is false in alternatives — that would hallucinate a capability the user hasn't set up.

tools.name: growth_fetch_person_profiles
tools.description: Fetch full LinkedIn person profiles for a list of LinkedIn URLs (e.g. https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe/). Returns the structured profile payload (full_name, headline, currentPosition[], experience[], education[], location, about, etc.) for each URL. S3-cached for 30 days per URL — repeat calls for the same URL are free. Bad/private URLs come back with `found: false`. Use this when you have LinkedIn URLs (from a CSV upload, find_people output, sales_nav export, etc.) and need full profile detail to drive personalization, AI filters, or enrichment. BY DEFAULT also returns each profile's recent posts (past 20 days, authored by THIS profile) on the result's `recent_posts[]` — costs +1 credit per profile, required by the personalization selector for Tier-A signal detection (recent posts, launches, talks). Set `with_recent_posts: false` to skip the post fetch and save the credit when you only need static profile data (e.g. routing / matching). Hard cap: 200 URLs per call. Never reveal vendor/actor details to the user.

linkedin_urls.description: List of LinkedIn person profile URLs (linkedin.com/in/{slug} or linkedin.com/pub/{slug}). Normalized + deduped internally. Cap 200.

skip_cache.description: If true, bypass the 30-day S3 cache and run a fresh fetch. Default false.

with_recent_posts.description: If true (DEFAULT), also fetch each profile's recent posts via RapidAPI profile_updates, filtered to the past `posts_within_days` days. Adds +1 credit per profile. Set false when you don't need post signal (saves the credit). Default true.

posts_within_days.description: Filter window for `recent_posts[]` (only used when `with_recent_posts` is true). Default 20 — matches the personalization selector's Tier-A recency cutoff. Range 1–180.

tools.name: growth_list_incubator_options
tools.description: List available incubators, or pass incubator_name to list its valid batch_ids. Use before growth_incubator_batch when the exact incubator or batch spelling is uncertain.

incubator_name.description: Optional incubator name. Omit to list incubators; pass a name to list batches.

tools.description: Data-native incubator batch job. Use when the user wants incubator/batch data back directly, without creating or editing a sequence. result_mode="companies" returns company rows; result_mode="people" finds contacts at those companies with target_title_tags using the same shared engine as the platform incubator source. Returns a composable job_id; poll with growth_get_job and export with growth_export_job_csv.

incubator_name.description: Incubator/program name, e.g. "Y Combinator" or "Techstars". Use growth_list_incubator_options for valid names.

batch_ids.description: One or more exact batch ids, e.g. ["W25"] or ["S24", "W25"].

result_mode.description: companies returns batch companies; people finds contacts at those companies.

target_title_tags.description: Required for people mode. Job-title filters, e.g. ["Founder", "CEO", "CTO"].

max_companies.description: Maximum batch companies to read. Default 1000, hard cap 5000.

max_contacts.description: Maximum contact rows in people mode. Default 500, hard cap 2000.

max_per_company.description: Maximum contacts per company in people mode. Default 3, hard cap 50.

wait_seconds.description: How long the MCP tool should poll before returning. Defaults to 30, max 120.
