tools.description: Data-native job posting contacts job. Use when the user wants hiring-related job posting and contact rows back directly, without creating or editing a sequence. Runs the same shared engine as the platform job_posting source and exports job_posting, contact, contact_skip, and contact_error rows. Returns a composable job_id; poll with growth_get_job and export with growth_export_job_csv.

job_title_tags.description: Required job posting search terms, e.g. ["Founding Engineer", "VP Sales"].

location_tags.description: Optional JSearch locations, e.g. ["United States", "San Francisco"].

days.description: Optional posting age window in days. Uses the platform job_posting mapping to JSearch date filters.

include_hiring_manager.description: Whether to emit hiring-manager contacts from LinkedIn job postings. Defaults true.

target_title_tags.description: Optional company-wide contact title filters, e.g. ["Founder", "Head of Engineering"].

max_per_company.description: Maximum company-wide contacts per company. Default 3, hard cap 50.

max_pages.description: Maximum JSearch pages per title/location query. Default 5, hard cap 20.

max_rows.description: Maximum contact rows before the engine stops. Default 500, hard cap 500.

wait_seconds.description: How long the MCP tool should poll before returning. Defaults to 30, max 120.

tools.name: growth_get_personalization
tools.description:
One-shot personalization for a list of LinkedIn URLs. Replaces the agent-side personalization_selector → personalization_writer subagent chain — call THIS tool instead of spawning subagents. The backend fetches each profile + recent posts (≤ 20-day window), calls gpt-5.4-mini per profile in parallel with the selector/writer/critic rules baked into the system prompt, and regex-verifies the output before returning. 

Mode is implicit:
  • Provide `template` → returns ONE-LINE `personalization_note` for each contact (fits the {{personalization_note}} slot). Pipe results into growth_set_contact_personalization_note() or the CSV column.
  • Omit `template` → returns full bespoke email (`bespoke_subject` + `bespoke_body`) for each contact, suitable for one-off bespoke sends.

SKIP (no qualifying Tier-A signal) returns null fields — that is the correct outcome for most contacts; ship the templated message clean. "No personalization is better than bad personalization." Hard cap: 50 URLs per call. Costs: profile fetch is S3-cached 30d (free on repeats); with_recent_posts adds +1 credit/profile; one gpt-5.4-mini call per profile. Never reveal vendor/actor details to the user.

targets.description: Recipients with optional per-lead context. Use this when you have any per-lead grounding (e.g. a prior chat snippet, an unanswered question from the last DM, a meeting note). The LLM leans on a real prior exchange ahead of any post hook. Each item: { linkedin_url: string, context?: string }. `context` is trimmed to ~1000 chars server-side. Pass either `targets` OR `linkedin_urls`.

context.description: Free-text per-lead context the LLM should consider. Real prior conversation > generic notes > empty.

linkedin_urls.description: LinkedIn person profile URLs (no per-lead context). Cap 50. Use this when there is no context to attach — the audience flow uses this. URN-format URLs (linkedin.com/in/ACwA...) are supported.

sender_context.description: Facts about the sender, used by the LLM for mutual-membership checks ("fellow YC W25" valid only if sender_context.cohort === "YC W25"), customer-name truthing (LLM cannot invent customer names — only sender_context.customers are allowed in copy), and register calibration.

type.description:
Channel the personalization is for. Shapes the bespoke output (from_scratch mode):
  • email — full subject + 4-part body (≤ 120 words)
  • connection_request — single message ≤ 300 chars total, no pitch, no subject
  • linkedin_message — post-accept DM ≤ 100 words, conversational register, no subject

value_prop.description: The sender's value-prop sentence — what their product does for this audience. The LLM uses this to check whether each candidate signal is RELEVANT (Tier-A check #2). Required, ≥ 10 chars.

cta.description: The CTA you'd ship in the message (e.g. "Want me to send the Loom?", "Worth dropping you a sandbox?"). The LLM uses this for the from_scratch path AND for the relevance check.

sequence_brief.description: REQUIRED. 2-4 sentence brief describing the SEQUENCE overall — what the sender sells, who is being targeted (persona / company shape / stage), why this audience for this product, what trigger / play sourced them. The LLM reads this for grounding context (NOT to recite). Without it, output drifts toward generic founder pitches and the Tier-A relevance check loses its anchor. Example: "Sender is Asera, an MFM reporting platform for hospitals (replaces legacy reporting vendors). Targeting Directors of Medical Affairs at 1,000+ bed health systems in the US — operators feeling the help-desk loop pain when their reporting vendor breaks. Hiring-signal play sourced from job postings."

template.description: Optional. When provided, switches to for_template mode — returns ONE-LINE personalization_note per contact that fits the {{personalization_note}} slot in this template. When omitted, returns a full bespoke output per contact in the shape of `type`.

today_iso.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to server-side today. Used by the recency filter.

posts_within_days.description: Recency window for Tier-A signals. Default 20 — matches the ≤ 20-day Tier-A cutoff.

tools.name: growth_qualify_rows
tools.description: Standalone AI-qualify rows from a local CSV file. Use this when the user already has CSV/list data and wants qualified data back; it does NOT create or edit a sequence. Primary input is csv_path to avoid sending hundreds of rows through chat. Processes at most 500 rows per job. IMPORTANT — chunk size auto-narrows for wide CSVs: the bridge rejects uploads over 5 MiB, so when rows are wide (long pitch / persona / description columns) the tool will use FEWER rows per chunk than max_rows. The response includes a `chunk_size` object with `requested_max_rows`, `effective_max_rows`, `byte_capped`, and a human-readable `reason`. When `byte_capped: true` the `note` explains the narrowing AND the `next_start_row` to continue from — just call again with that start_row, do not fight the narrowing by lowering max_rows yourself. Returns job_id, progress, mapping summary, chunk_size info, and a small preview. Use growth_get_job to poll and growth_export_job_csv to download the result CSV.

csv_path.description: Absolute path to the CSV to qualify. Required.

prompt.description: Qualification/filter prompt, e.g. "pass VP Sales or revenue leaders at B2B SaaS companies".

entity_kind.description: What each CSV row represents. Use "contact" for people/leads, "company" for account/company CSVs, and "row" for generic/non-GTM records. Defaults to "contact".

field_mapping.description: Optional explicit mapping from canonical field key to CSV header, e.g. {"contact_job_title":"Title","company_name":"Company"}.

visible_columns.description: Optional CSV columns to show the evaluator. Defaults to all columns in the selected chunk.

start_row.description: 1-indexed data-row offset to process. Defaults to 1. Use next_start_row from the previous response to continue a large CSV.

max_rows.description: Rows to process in this job. Defaults to 500 and is capped at 500.

wait_seconds.description: How long the MCP tool should poll before returning. Defaults to 30, max 120.

tools.name: growth_get_job
tools.description: Get status and a page of rows for any generic composable MCP job, including growth_qualify_rows and growth_targeted_search_people. Use this instead of per-tool status tools when you have a job_id.

job_id.description: Job id returned by a composable MCP tool.

offset.description: 0-indexed row offset for result rows. Defaults to 0.

limit.description: Rows to return. Defaults to 20, max 100.

tools.name: growth_export_job_csv
tools.description: Download the full CSV artifact for a completed composable MCP job to local disk. Use after growth_get_job shows completed, or call directly and handle "not available yet".

job_id.description: Job id returned by a composable MCP tool.

output_path.description: Optional absolute local path to write. Defaults to /tmp/flage-mcp-jobs/...

tools.name: growth_targeted_search_people
tools.description: Data-native targeted LinkedIn people search. Use when the user wants people data back directly, without creating or editing a sequence. Filters by job_title_tags, location_tags, and/or LinkedIn company URLs. For large company URL lists such as 500 companies, pass company_linkedin_urls_csv_path instead of inline arrays. Returns a composable job_id; poll with growth_get_job and export with growth_export_job_csv.

job_title_tags.description: Current job-title filters, e.g. ["VP Sales", "Head of Revenue"].

location_tags.description: Location filters accepted by the targeted search backend, e.g. ["United States", "San Francisco Bay Area"].

company_linkedin_urls.description: Small inline list of LinkedIn company or school URLs. Use company_linkedin_urls_csv_path for large lists.

company_linkedin_urls_csv_path.description: Absolute path to CSV / text / JSON containing linkedin.com/company/* or linkedin.com/school/* URLs. Required for large lists.

max_rows.description: Maximum profiles to return. Default 500, hard cap 500.

wait_seconds.description: How long the MCP tool should poll before returning. Defaults to 30, max 120.

tools.name: growth_run_sequence_personalization
tools.description:
Run personalization on a sequence audience — the same flow the in-product "Personalize" button triggers. Two modes:
  • dry_run=true (default): preview on a sample. If `contact_ids` is supplied, those are used (capped by max_contacts). Otherwise the bridge samples max_contacts random contacts from the audience. Nothing is written.
  • dry_run=false: walks the full audience and writes the generated note onto contact_enrichments_jsonb.personalization_note for each contact. `contact_ids` is ignored in this mode.
Returns {workflow_id} immediately — poll growth_get_sequence_personalization_progress until finished:true to read the per-contact results. The personalization config (sender context, value prop, CTA, sequence brief) is read from the sequence itself; no need to pass it in. Default max_contacts is 10 (cap 1000). When the audience is empty or the sequence has no sources, returns `workflow_id: ""` with a `reason` instead of starting a workflow.

sequence_id.description: The sequence whose audience to personalize. Must already have a personalization config.

dry_run.description: When true (default), runs a preview on a sample without writing notes. When false, walks the full audience and writes notes — equivalent to the in-product "Run for all" action.

contact_ids.description: Optional. Specific contacts to preview against (only honored when dry_run=true). When omitted, the bridge picks max_contacts random audience contacts.

max_contacts.description: Sample size for dry_run previews. Default 10, max 1000.

tools.name: growth_get_sequence_personalization_progress
tools.description: Snapshot of a personalization workflow started by growth_run_sequence_personalization. Poll repeatedly until `finished: true`. While running, returns the latest `status` ("running"|"pending") and `latest_step` (e.g. "fetching_and_matching", "generating_notes"). When `finished: true` and `failed: false`, `results` is the per-contact list — each row has contact_id, contact_full_name, note (the generated personalization line; empty when SKIP), skipped_reason, written. `failed: true` surfaces `error_message`. `summary` (total/written/skipped/with_note) is included only on successful completion.

tools.name: growth_extract_person_attributes
tools.description:
Extract voice-calibration attributes from LinkedIn profiles for cold-outreach copy. Returns career_stage, generation, register_recommendation, country, and a 1-2 sentence connection_story per profile. It does not return shared-affiliation vectors; use growth_suggest_sender for sender-lead routing.

**Use the result as voice CALIBRATION, never as facts to cite.** The copy writer reads these to shape register / generation / locale / angle, but NEVER quotes attribute values back to the recipient. "I see you went to MIT therefore..." is the canonical anti-pattern — banned. See attribute_extractor.md for the calibration-not-citation rule.

When to call: individual outreach OR small-batch sequence (≤ 20 targets) OR enterprise sequence (≤ 100 targets, where personalization is mandatory). Skip for high-volume SMB sequences (cost + latency not worth it).

sender_context is REQUIRED for sender-aware calibration. Pass at minimum: sender_name, sender_company, sender_role. Add sender_school, sender_company_description, sender_affiliations (e.g. ["YC W22", "ex-Stripe"]) when available.

linkedin_urls.description: List of target LinkedIn person URLs. Normalized + deduped internally. Cap 100.

sender_context.description: Sender context — required for mutual-membership detection. Suggested fields: { sender_name, sender_company, sender_role, sender_school, sender_company_description, sender_affiliations: ["YC W22", ...] }. Free-shape — pass whatever the LLM should consider when checking whether the sender shares an affiliation with each target.

tools.name: growth_suggest_sender
tools.description:
Pick the best-matched sender from a candidate pool for a given lead. Pass the lead's LinkedIn URL and a list of candidate senders (each with sender_id + their own LinkedIn URL). Returns:

- `result: "matched"` + `suggested_sender_id` — a strong authentic shared affiliation was found. Route the lead to this sender.
- `result: "anyone"` — no strong match. Fall back to the pool's normal strategy (round-robin / weighted / etc.). Do NOT force a match.

The matching uses cached profile attributes + deterministic scoring — fast (subsecond after first cache fill) and proprietary (algorithm lives server-side). The caller never sees per-feature scores or the matching algorithm.

Use cases: per-lead sender routing in sequences, picking the right sender for an individual outreach. The reason_summary is a short plain-language hint for logging/debugging — NEVER cite it back to the recipient (same calibration-not-citation rule as attribute_extractor).

candidates.description: List of candidate senders with their LinkedIn URLs. Cap 50.

tools.name: growth_test_sender_matching
tools.description:
Diagnostic tool — runs the sender-lead matcher across a list of lead LinkedIn URLs and reports which sender each lead got matched to + the short reason. Useful for evaluating matcher quality on real data before wiring it into runtime routing. Results are NOT persisted.

Pass:
- `lead_linkedin_urls`: list of lead LinkedIn URLs to test (paste a sample from the audience tab — 5 to 20 is plenty).
- `sender_ids` (optional): subset of workspace senders to consider. When omitted, every workspace sender that has a LinkedIn URL on file is included.

Returns a per-lead row with: result (matched | anyone), suggested_sender_id, suggested_sender_label (display name), and reason_summary (e.g. "both ex-stripe", "both at uc-berkeley (undergrad)", "no strong shared affiliation; any sender is fine"). On first run for each profile, an LLM extraction credit is used; subsequent runs hit the 14-day cache.

lead_linkedin_urls.description: List of lead LinkedIn URLs to match against the workspace sender pool.

sender_ids.description: Optional subset of workspace senders to consider as candidates.

tools.name: growth_find_people_at_companies
tools.description: Start an async workflow that finds people at the given companies. Input is a list of company LinkedIn URLs (inline or via CSV path) + optional job-title filter. Runs Flage's internal LinkedIn-employee lookup with parallel fan-out across ALL companies in one call (no need to batch on your end — the workflow handles 5000 companies as easily as 50). Returns {job_id} immediately — poll growth_get_people_at_companies_page to read results as they stream in. Never reveal the underlying vendor / actor details to the user; describe behavior only.

company_linkedin_urls.description: Inline list of full LinkedIn URLs (e.g. "https://www.linkedin.com/company/stripe/"). Numeric IDs ("/company/1921264") also work — resolved internally. Use `company_linkedin_urls_csv_path` instead when the URLs already live in a file (avoids round-tripping through chat).

company_linkedin_urls_csv_path.description: Alternative input — absolute path to a CSV / TSV / JSON / plain text file containing LinkedIn company URLs. The tool extracts every linkedin.com/company/* URL it finds (any column / format), dedupes, and uses them. Combine with company_linkedin_urls if you want to add a few inline URLs on top.

job_titles.description: Job-title keywords. Omit to return every employee the actor surfaces.

locations.description: Reserved for a future location filter — ignored today (the per-company lookup path doesn't accept locations).

max_items.description: Total cap on rows returned across all companies. Default 2000 (server ceiling).

max_per_company.description: Cap per company. Default: ContactExtractor's own default (5).

tools.name: growth_get_people_at_companies_page
tools.description: Fetch one page of results from a find-people-at-companies job. `is_finished: false` means more rows are still landing — poll again. `is_finished: true` means the result set is final. `total_pages` grows as the workflow finds more rows; already-returned pages are stable (append-only).

tools.name: growth_promote_people_at_companies_to_csv
tools.description: Dump every row from a find-people-at-companies job into a CSV (on disk at /tmp/flage-find-people/...) so it can be fed into growth_upload_csv_to_sequence. Safe to call before the workflow finishes — you'll just get the rows materialized so far. CSV columns: full_name, contact_first_name/last_name/job_title/linkedin_url/location, company_name, company_linkedin_url, source_company_linkedin_url.

label.description: Optional label used in the CSV filename.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_list_sessions
tools.description:
Enumerate every Chrome tab open on linkedin.com (across all Chrome profiles + windows) and report which LinkedIn account is logged in to each. Returns `[{ session_id, viewer: { public_identifier, first_name, last_name }, url }]`.

Use this **before** any send_connect / send_message / list_threads / get_messages call when the user might have more than one LinkedIn account active. Pass the chosen `session_id` back to those tools to target the right account.

If no LinkedIn tabs are open, returns an empty list — the action tools will then open a fresh `linkedin.com/feed/` tab on call.

Read-only.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_send_connect
tools.description:
**PREFER A SEQUENCE OVER ONE-OFF SENDS.** For anything beyond a single ad-hoc invite, build a sequence with `growth_create_sequence_draft` — sequences pace sends across days within LinkedIn's safe limits, support multi-step follow-ups, and obey the same per-sender daily / weekly caps. Use this tool only for genuine one-offs.

Queues a LinkedIn connection request through the user's connected Unipile sender (the same sender used by sequences). The backend writes a durable outbound intent; a Temporal drainer sends it when `scheduled_at` is due, pacing/quota allow, and sender availability checks pass.

**Returns** `{id, status: 'queued', sender_account_id, requested_at, scheduled_at}`. Status flips to `sent` or `failed` once the drainer runs; later acceptance/reply facts appear on `accepted_at` / `replied_at`. Poll `growth_linkedin_get_send_status`.

**Args:** `public_identifier` (vanity slug from `/in/<slug>`). Optional `note` (≤300 chars; non-Premium senders silently drop it per Unipile). Optional `scheduled_at` must be timezone-aware ISO 8601; omit to queue immediately. Optional `sender_account_id` to disambiguate when more than one LinkedIn sender is connected.

**Externally-visible action — confirm with the user before calling.**

sender_account_id.description: Optional. Specific connected LinkedIn sender_account.id when more than one is connected.

scheduled_at.description: Optional timezone-aware ISO 8601 timestamp, e.g. 2026-05-06T15:00:00-07:00. Omit to queue immediately.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Pass to dedupe retries — repeat calls return the existing outbox row.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_send_message
tools.description:
**PREFER A SEQUENCE OVER ONE-OFF SENDS.** For multi-recipient or multi-step outreach, build a sequence instead. This tool is for single one-off DMs only.

Queues a LinkedIn DM through the user's connected Unipile sender. Backend behavior is identical to `growth_linkedin_send_connect` — durable outbound intent, optional schedule, drainer send, shared per-sender daily / weekly cap with sequence sends.

**Returns** `{id, status: 'queued', sender_account_id, requested_at, scheduled_at}`. Poll `growth_linkedin_get_send_status` for `sent_at`, `failed`, and later `replied_at`.

**Externally-visible action — confirm with the user before calling.** Recipient should already be a 1st-degree connection (Unipile / LinkedIn reject DMs to non-connections from a free account).

sender_account_id.description: Optional. Specific connected LinkedIn sender_account.id when more than one is connected.

scheduled_at.description: Optional timezone-aware ISO 8601 timestamp, e.g. 2026-05-06T15:00:00-07:00. Omit to queue immediately.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_get_send_status
tools.description:
Checks a one-off LinkedIn send created by `growth_linkedin_send_connect` or `growth_linkedin_send_message`. Returns provider-send lifecycle plus engagement fields: `queued`, `sent`, `failed`, `scheduled_at`, `next_eligible_at`, `sent_at`, `accepted_at`, `replied_at`, and `detail`.

Use this for manual one-off sends only. Sequence sends are tracked through sequence/progress tools.

intent_id.description: The `id` returned by growth_linkedin_send_connect or growth_linkedin_send_message.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_get_messages
tools.description:
Fetch the message thread with a specific person (or by conversation URN). Pass `public_identifier` and the tool finds the existing 1:1 conversation, or pass `conversation_urn` directly.

**Multi-account safety:** pass `session_id` from `growth_linkedin_list_sessions` when more than one LinkedIn tab is open.

Reads the user's real LinkedIn inbox — confirm before calling.

public_identifier.description: Vanity slug of the other participant.

conversation_urn.description: Optional. If you already have the conversation URN (from `growth_linkedin_list_threads`), pass it to skip the lookup.

session_id.description: Optional opaque session identifier from `growth_linkedin_list_sessions` (e.g. "w1t3"). When the user has multiple LinkedIn tabs open across Chrome profiles, you MUST pass this to target the right account. Auto-picked when only one LinkedIn tab is open.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_list_threads
tools.description:
List the user's recent LinkedIn message threads (inbox). Returns each thread's `entityUrn` (use as `conversation_urn` in `growth_linkedin_get_messages`) and participant names.

**Multi-account safety:** pass `session_id` from `growth_linkedin_list_sessions` when more than one LinkedIn tab is open.

Reads the user's real LinkedIn inbox — confirm before calling.

session_id.description: Optional opaque session identifier from `growth_linkedin_list_sessions` (e.g. "w1t3"). When the user has multiple LinkedIn tabs open across Chrome profiles, you MUST pass this to target the right account. Auto-picked when only one LinkedIn tab is open.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_get_post
tools.description:
Fetch a LinkedIn post by URL (`https://www.linkedin.com/posts/...`), feed-update URL, raw `urn:li:activity:N`, or just the numeric id. Hits Voyager `/feed/updates/<urn>` from the user's logged-in Chrome tab — same approach as the post-reactor audience source uses, but for one specific post on demand.

Returns `{ urn, text, author: { name, public_identifier }, counters: { reactions, comments, reposts } }`. Read-only, **does not** count toward the LinkedIn write cap.

**Multi-account safety:** pass `session_id` from `growth_linkedin_list_sessions` when more than one LinkedIn tab is open. Auto-picked when only one tab is open.

post.description: LinkedIn post URL, feed-update URL, urn:li:activity:N, or the numeric id.

session_id.description: Optional opaque session identifier from `growth_linkedin_list_sessions` (e.g. "w1t3"). When the user has multiple LinkedIn tabs open across Chrome profiles, you MUST pass this to target the right account. Auto-picked when only one LinkedIn tab is open.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_search_posts
tools.description:
Search LinkedIn posts (the same content search you get at `linkedin.com/search/results/content/`) via the user's connected LinkedIn sender. Powered by Unipile classic search (`api: classic, category: posts`).

**Sender selection:** auto-picks when only one connected LinkedIn sender exists. Otherwise pass `sender_account_id` (the `senders.accounts[].id` from `growth_list_senders`) to choose which account performs the search.

**Filters** mirror the LinkedIn UI filter panel:
- `keywords` — search query.
- `date_posted` — `past_24h` | `past_week` | `past_month`.
- `content_type` — `videos` | `images` | `live_videos` | `job_posts` | `documents`.
- `sort_by` — `date` (latest) | `relevance` (top match).
- `posted_by` — `me` | `my_network` | `1st_connections` | `following`.
- `from_member` — array of LinkedIn member identifiers (vanity slug or URN).
- `from_company` — array of LinkedIn company identifiers (vanity slug or URN).
- `author_keywords` — restrict to posts whose author headline matches (e.g. `"CEO"`).
- `extra_filters` — passthrough object for any other Unipile field.

**Pagination:** pass `cursor` from the previous response to page. `limit` caps results per call (Unipile classic max: 50).

Read-only — does NOT count toward the LinkedIn write hourly cap. Returns `{ items, cursor, sender_account_id, unipile_account_id }`.

date_posted.description: Restrict to posts within this window.

content_type.description: Restrict to a specific content type.

sort_by.description: `date` = latest (LinkedIn UI default for date filter). `relevance` = top match.

from_member.description: LinkedIn member identifiers (vanity slug or URN) to restrict to.

from_company.description: LinkedIn company identifiers (vanity slug or URN) to restrict to.

author_keywords.description: Restrict to authors whose headline matches (Unipile's `author.keywords`).

extra_filters.description: Passthrough for any additional Unipile fields not modeled above.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

limit.description: Max results per call. Unipile classic caps at 50.

sender_account_id.description: Optional but required when multiple LinkedIn senders are connected. Pass `senders.accounts[].id` from `growth_list_senders`.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_search_people_start
tools.description:
Kick off a paginated LinkedIn classic-people search (the same people search you get at `linkedin.com/search/results/people/`) as a background Temporal job. Returns a `job_id` immediately — DO NOT block; poll `growth_linkedin_search_people_get_page` until `is_finished=true` (or read partial results as pages come in).

Powered by Unipile (`api: classic, category: people`). Page size is fixed at 10 (Unipile classic cap). Workflow sleeps 3-4s between page fetches to mimic human pacing — a 15-page run takes roughly 45-75s wall clock.

**Sender selection:** auto-picks when only one connected LinkedIn sender exists. Otherwise pass `sender_account_id` (the `senders.accounts[].id` from `growth_list_senders`).

**Filters:**
- `keywords` — search query (boolean modifiers supported, e.g. `growth AND lead NOT manager`).
- `network` — array of LinkedIn network-distance codes: `F` (1st-degree), `S` (2nd-degree), `O` (3rd+/out-of-network). Example: `["S"]` matches the LinkedIn URL `?network=%5B%22S%22%5D`.
- `location` — array of place names. Mapped to LinkedIn `geoUrn` IDs server-side. Currently supported:
    *Countries:* France, Belgium, Spain, England, Germany, Italy, United States, Canada, Australia, India, China, Japan, Brazil, Mexico, Netherlands, Singapore, Switzerland, Sweden, South Korea, Russia, United Arab Emirates.
    *US metros / cities / states:* San Francisco Bay Area, San Francisco, California, United States; New York City Metropolitan Area; New York, United States; Boston, Massachusetts, United States.
    Use the most specific name that matches the user's intent. For any place not on this list, pass the LinkedIn geo ID directly via `extra_filters: { location: ["<id>"] }`.
- `extra_filters` — passthrough object for any other Unipile field (industry, current_company, school, etc.) or extra location IDs.

Returns `{ job_id, workflow_id, sender_account_id, unipile_account_id }`. Read-only — does NOT count toward the LinkedIn write hourly cap.

location.description: Place names to filter by. Resolved to LinkedIn geo IDs server-side. For unsupported places, pass IDs via `extra_filters.location` instead.

extra_filters.description: Passthrough for any additional Unipile fields not modeled above.

max_pages.description: Pages to fetch (10 results/page). 1-15. Workflow sleeps 3-4s between fetches.

sender_account_id.description: Optional but required when multiple LinkedIn senders are connected. Pass `senders.accounts[].id` from `growth_list_senders`.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_search_people_get_page
tools.description:
Read a page of results from a LinkedIn people-search job started via `growth_linkedin_search_people_start`. Each call returns up to `page_size` people plus a status snapshot.

**Polling pattern:**
1. Call `growth_linkedin_search_people_start`, save `job_id`.
2. Call this tool with `job_id, page=1` every ~5s until `is_finished=true`. Partial results are visible during the run — `pages_fetched` tells you how far the workflow has progressed (out of `pages_planned`).
3. When `total_count > page_size`, increment `page` to drain the rest.

Returns `{ people, page, page_size, total_count, total_pages, pages_fetched, pages_planned, is_finished }`. If the workflow `failed`, `is_finished=true` with `error_message` populated via `/status` (call `growth_linkedin_search_people_get_page` first; if zero results and finished, the search hit an error — surface it to the user).

page_size.description: Items per page (default 50). Independent of the workflow's internal 10/page Unipile fetch.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_get_contact_relationship
tools.description:
Look up a LinkedIn person from the connected sender's vantage point. Returns name, headline, location, occupation, **network distance** (`SELF` / `DISTANCE_1` = 1st-degree connection / `DISTANCE_2` / `DISTANCE_3` / `OUT_OF_NETWORK`), `is_connection` boolean (true iff 1st-degree or self), and an `id` you pass to `growth_linkedin_get_chat_history` for past message history.

**Sender selection:** auto-picks when only one connected LinkedIn sender exists. Otherwise pass `sender_account_id`.

**Use this BEFORE sending a connect / DM** to know whether you're already connected (skip the connect, go straight to DM) or 2nd-degree (connect first), and to ground any claim about the person in real profile data instead of guessing from a slug.

Powered by Unipile's `GET /users/{public_identifier}` endpoint. Read-only, doesn't count toward the LinkedIn write hourly cap.

linkedin_url_or_slug.description: LinkedIn profile URL (`https://www.linkedin.com/in/<slug>/`) or bare public_identifier slug.

sender_account_id.description: Optional. Required when multiple LinkedIn senders are connected.

tools.name: growth_linkedin_get_chat_history
tools.description:
List every message the connected sender has exchanged with this person across all 1:1 LinkedIn chats. **`items[0]` is the most recent message.** Each message carries `text`, `timestamp` (ISO 8601), `is_sender` (1 = we sent it, 0 = they sent it), `chat_id`, `attachments`, `message_type` (MESSAGE / INVITATION / INMAIL / etc.), and `seen` status.

**Pagination:** auto-drains up to 5 pages × 250 messages = 1250-message ceiling per call (one second pacing between pages). LinkedIn 1:1 chats almost never exceed that. If you genuinely need to go deeper, pass `cursor` from a previous response to resume.

**`id`** must be the `id` returned by `growth_linkedin_get_contact_relationship` (LinkedIn member URN — Unipile accepts it as `provider_id`).

**Use this after `get_contact_relationship`** to see whether you've talked before, what was said, and how recent the last touch was — gives the agent the full conversation context before deciding to follow up vs. cold-DM vs. skip.

Returns `{ items, cursor, pages_fetched, sender_account_id, unipile_account_id }`. Empty `items` = no chat history with this person.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor — only needed to resume past the 5-page (1250-message) default drain.

sender_account_id.description: Optional. Required when multiple LinkedIn senders are connected.

tools.name: growth_resolve_company_linkedin_urls
tools.description:
Resolve a list of company domains to their LinkedIn company URLs (e.g. acme.com -> https://www.linkedin.com/company/acme). Runs an async backend workflow that resolves each domain to its company page on LinkedIn. Polls until finished, then returns a 4-column bridge CSV (company_domain, company_linkedin_url, source, status).

Use this whenever you have domains (Clay jobs CSV, Crunchbase export, manual list, etc.) and need real LinkedIn URLs to feed into growth_find_people_at_companies — guessing slugs from company names silently drops 10-25% of rows. To carry domain + name through to the final people CSV, then pass the bridge CSV through growth_join_csv_files (left = bridge, right = people CSV, on=company_linkedin_url, normalize_key=linkedin_url).

domains.description: List of company domains. Bare hosts ("acme.com") and full URLs ("https://acme.com/about") both work — normalized internally. Deduped before lookup. Capped at 2000 per call.

tools.name: growth_resolve_company_domains
tools.description:
Resolve a list of company names to their canonical website domains. For each name, the workflow searches the web, drops aggregator and directory hosts (linkedin, yelp, wikipedia, indeed, glassdoor, crunchbase, bbb, ...), then picks the candidate that is the company's actual website (or "none" if no candidate clearly belongs to that firm). Polls until the workflow finishes, then returns a 6-column bridge CSV (company_name, company_location, company_domain, source, status, matched_url).

Use this whenever you have a list of company names without domains. The tool is upstream-agnostic: works for names from a CSV upload, a Chrome scrape of a public directory, a Clay search, a manual list, anywhere. `location` (city / state / country) is OPTIONAL — pass it for common firm names ("Smith & Co LLP") to disambiguate, skip it for unique names ("Stripe", "Datadog") where it adds nothing. Don't fabricate location; a wrong location is worse than none. Up to 2000 companies per call.

location.description: Optional location hint (e.g. "Boise, ID", "London, UK"). Strongly recommended for common firm names — without it, the resolver may pick the wrong company.

companies.description: Companies to resolve. Each entry needs a `name`; pass `location` whenever you have one. Deduped internally on (name, location). Capped at 2000 per call.

tools.name: growth_get_sequence_template
tools.description: Return a canonical sequence template. Call this BEFORE drafting copy. Pass `channel_mix` to pick the shape: `mix` (default, branched email+LinkedIn), `email_only` (3-touch email cadence, no LinkedIn), `linkedin_only` (connection request + post-accept DM, no email). The agent should ALWAYS ask the user up front which mix they want before fetching the template — default to `mix` unless they say otherwise. Returns the step shape + slot_rules + copy guardrails. Fill slots by asking the user targeted questions (never invent answers), then call growth_create_sequence_draft. Allowed {{var}} names: first_name, last_name, company_name, sender_first_name, sender_last_name, sender_company_name, personalization_note.

channel_mix.description: Channel topology. `mix` (default) fires an email first, then a LinkedIn connection request with branches (DM on accept, email follow-up on reject). `email_only` is 3 emails spaced 72h / 120h apart — no LinkedIn. `linkedin_only` sends a connection request, then a LinkedIn DM on accept; the on_not_accepted branch is empty because there is no fallback channel.

tools.name: growth_ensure_workspace
tools.description: Ensure the current user has a workspace. Creates one if this is a brand-new anonymous user. Returns the workspace slug. Safe to call repeatedly. Pass `workspace_id` (id or slug) to switch the active workspace context — subsequent tool calls in this session will route to that workspace.

workspace_id.description: Optional workspace id or slug to switch to. Use a value from `workspaces` returned by growth_session_init / growth_auth_status. When omitted, returns the current workspace (creating one if anonymous).

tools.name: growth_list_sequences
tools.description: List all sequences in the current workspace.

tools.name: growth_get_plans
tools.description: Return the purchasable Verbiflow plan catalog (Starter / Pro / Scale) with current pricing, bundled seats, and credit caps. No auth required and no Stripe round-trip — safe to call before the user has a workspace or to answer "what plans do you have?" directly. Source of truth is backend `PLAN_CONFIG`, so prices stay in sync if they change. Response: { plans: [{ plan_tier, display_name, price_cents, bundled_seats, credits_limit }], default_plan_tier }.

tools.name: growth_billing_status
tools.description: Check the current workspace's plan tier and subscription state. Call this silently right before publishing a sequence (not earlier — no need to nag users who are still drafting). Response includes: { has_workspace_subscription: bool, workspace_subscription_status, plan_tier: "free" | "legacy" | "starter" | "pro" | "scale" | null, plan_display_name, plan_bundled_seats, plan_credits_limit, purchasable_plans: [{ plan_tier, display_name, price_cents, bundled_seats, credits_limit }] }. If `plan_tier === "free"` the user has never paid — they cannot publish a sequence. Show them `purchasable_plans`, ask which one fits (Starter / Pro / Scale), then call `growth_get_checkout_url` with that `plan_tier` and hand them the Stripe link.

tools.name: growth_get_checkout_url
tools.description: Generate a Stripe Checkout URL for the current workspace subscription on a specific plan tier. Use this when `growth_billing_status` reports `plan_tier === "free"` (or no active subscription) AND the user has told you which plan they want. Returns `{ checkout_url }` — hand that URL to the user verbatim; one click opens hosted Stripe checkout, and after success Stripe redirects them back to `success_url`. Optional `promo_code` applies a discount.

plan_tier.description: Which plan to subscribe to. Pick from `purchasable_plans` returned by `growth_billing_status`. Required unless you want the backend default (Starter). Pricing/seats/credits live on each plan in `purchasable_plans` — show those numbers to the user before picking.

promo_code.description: Optional Stripe promo code to apply at checkout.

next_path.description: In-app path Stripe redirects the user to after successful checkout. Defaults to the sequences list for the current workspace. Must start with "/".

tools.name: growth_list_senders
tools.description: Return the viewer's senders + their channel accounts. A sender is the person/identity doing the sending; each sender has one or more accounts (email mailbox, LinkedIn account). Use this to decide whether the user needs to connect an email mailbox or LinkedIn before publishing / sandbox-sending. Response shape: array of { sender_id, display_name, email, accounts: [{ channel: "email"|"linkedin", provider, connection_status, health_status, ...}] }. A fully-connected email account has connection_status !== "disconnected" / "not_connected". Call this silently before prompting the user to connect — only ask if the relevant channel is actually missing, and return the builder senders URL for them to connect via the web UI.

tools.name: growth_list_audience_sources
tools.description: Return the live registry of audience source kinds Flage supports + the attributes each emits per lead. ALWAYS call this before proposing an ICP or picking a source_kind for growth_create_sequence_draft — the list is the authoritative ground truth, hardcoding sources in the skill goes stale. Response shape: { sources: [{kind, default_display_name, description, default_config, output_columns: [{field_key, display_name}], ui_state, ...}], enrichment_attributes: [{key, attribute_type, note}], unsupported_facets: [string] }. Use `output_columns` + `enrichment_attributes` to decide what filters are possible. If the ICP requires a facet in `unsupported_facets` (funding_stage, revenue, tech_stack, etc.), DO NOT propose it unless the user explicitly asks.

tools.name: growth_get_sequence
tools.description: Full detail of a sequence — name, state, steps, lead count, metrics, and web_url.

tools.name: growth_create_sequence_draft
tools.description: Create a new sequence draft. Pass a name, an ordered list of steps, and optionally the audience source. Each step has channel (email | linkedin_connection | linkedin_message), body, subject (email only), wait_hours (delay before this step). LinkedIn connection-request steps can branch via on_accepted (continues on LinkedIn) and on_not_accepted (falls back to email). audience_source picks the right lead pipeline: incubator (YC), linkedin_post_reactors, linkedin_network, job_posting, targeted_search, conference_attendees, sales_nav_url, luma_events, or manual (CSV fallback). Never ship "manual" if a better source fits the ICP.

workspace_id.description: Optional target workspace (id or slug). Required when the user belongs to more than one workspace and you need the draft to land in a specific one — without it, the draft goes to whatever workspace is currently active in the MCP session. Use a value from `workspaces` returned by growth_session_init / growth_auth_status.

channel.description: email = cold outreach (has subject + body). reply_email = threaded follow-up, NO subject — send layer auto-prepends Re: and sets In-Reply-To to the preceding email step. Constraint: a reply_email step is ONLY valid if the immediately-preceding step in the same chain is another email or reply_email — it has no anchor otherwise and will be rejected. linkedin_connection = LinkedIn connect request with note. linkedin_message = DM after accept. Use reply_email for any mid-sequence follow-up that should thread under step 1; do NOT use email with a manual re: prefix.

on_accepted.description: Branch sub-chain that fires when a LinkedIn connection request is accepted. Use for keeping the recipient on LinkedIn (typical: wait → linkedin_message).

on_not_accepted.description: Branch sub-chain that fires when the LinkedIn connection request is NOT accepted (timeout). Use for falling back to email (typical: wait → email).

audience_source.description: Audience source config. Choose the source_kind that matches the ICP (e.g. "incubator" for YC, "linkedin_post_reactors" for founder-post targets). Only use "manual" if the user explicitly has their own CSV.

initial_filter.description: FilterNode inserted between the audience source and the first action step. Gates leads by ICP-fit so dirty source pools do not burn sends on off-ICP leads. REQUIRED whenever the user has any ICP narrowing criteria (almost always). Only mode exposed: natural-language `ai_filter_prompt`. The runtime runs an LLM per lead against the prompt, looking at company_description, contact_job_title, and other enriched fields, and returns pass/fail. The prompt MUST cover FIVE parts: (1) sequence context — what the sender is selling and to whom (1-2 sentences at the top, otherwise the per-lead LLM filters in a vacuum and lets through anyone whose title superficially matches), (2) company INCLUDE, (3) company EXCLUDE, (4) contact INCLUDE, (5) contact EXCLUDE. Negative examples materially improve filter quality.

label.description: Display label for the Matched branch (default "Matched").

ai_filter_prompt.description: Natural-language ICP description. MUST start with 1-2 sentences naming what the sender sells and to whom (the per-lead filter LLM has no other awareness of the pitch). Then INCLUDE + EXCLUDE for BOTH company and contact. Example: "This sequence pitches Acme (developer-platform observability for backend teams) to Series A-C B2B SaaS companies whose engineering org is large enough to feel pain from siloed logs/metrics/traces. Keep only B2B SaaS companies building developer tools or internal-ops software, 10-100 employees. Exclude crypto, web3, consumer apps, e-commerce, marketplaces, agencies, consultancies, hardware. For contacts, keep only founders, co-founders, CEOs, CTOs, or founding team members. Exclude investors, advisors, interns, and non-founding engineers."

tools.name: growth_update_sequence_steps
tools.description: Replace the email / LinkedIn step chain on an existing sequence draft. Use this AFTER growth_create_sequence_draft whenever you rewrite copy with the user — edits in chat are not persistent until you call this tool. The audience source, filter prompt, sender selection, and schedule are preserved untouched; only the step chain is rebuilt. Optimistic concurrency is handled internally (tool reads draft_version before writing), so the agent just passes the new steps. Steps use the same shape as growth_create_sequence_draft: channel, subject (email only), body, wait_hours, on_accepted / on_not_accepted branches. Returns the refreshed sequence detail + web_url.

tools.name: growth_update_source_config
tools.description: Patch the config on an existing source node ingress — used to edit source-specific fields like `job_title_tags` (job_posting), `batch_id` / `target_title_tags` (incubator), `query` / `interaction_types` (linkedin_post_reactors), `keyword_tags` / `from_date` / `to_date` (conference_attendees), `job_title_tags` / `location_tags` / `company_linkedin_urls` (targeted_search), etc. Accepts a PARTIAL patch: keys you pass override the current ingress config, keys you omit are preserved from the existing config. The tool reads the current source node via growth_get_sequence, merges your patch, and PATCHes the full merged config back. Auto-picks the source_node_id and ingress_id when the sequence has exactly one active source / ingress — pass them explicitly only when there are multiple. Pass `source_kind` in the config to swap the ingress to a different kind (e.g. job_posting → manual for CSV Import). When swapping kinds, pass only the fields valid for the new kind — stale keys from the old kind will be dropped by the backend schema.

source_node_id.description: Optional. Auto-detected when the sequence has exactly one source node. Required when the sequence has multiple source nodes.

ingress_id.description: Optional. Auto-detected when the source has exactly one active ingress. Required when the source has multiple ingresses.

tools.name: growth_delete_sequence_lead_list
tools.description: Detach an uploaded lead list (CSV import) from a sequence draft. Use when a stale or wrong list is still attached alongside the current audience — e.g. an old big-co list left over from an earlier upload. Resolves the lead_list_id from the sequence (call growth_get_sequence first to see attached lists if you don't already have the id). Sequence must be in draft state; published sequences must be edited in the builder. Returns the remaining lead_list_ids so you can confirm the right one was removed.

sequence_id.description: The sequence id (uuid) the lead list is attached to.

lead_list_id.description: The lead list id (uuid) to detach. Get it from growth_get_sequence — attached lead lists appear under the source node's audience refs.

tools.name: growth_set_personalization_note
tools.description:
Write a per-recipient `personalization_note` value onto a sequence row. AUTO-ROUTES based on which identifiers you pass:
  • Pass `contact_id` → writes to the materialized contact_row (after the source has run / been materialized).
  • Pass `source_run_id` + `row_identifier` → writes to the staging row (BEFORE the source has materialized — used for incubator pulls, linkedin_post_reactors, hiring-signal sources, or manual CSV pre-publish where contacts don't exist yet but you have preview rows).
In both cases, the value flows into `audience_attributes` at enrollment time and becomes the `{{personalization_note}}` template variable at send time. Pass an empty string to clear the slot — the runtime substitutes "" and the surrounding paragraph collapses cleanly.

Important: edits made AFTER a contact is enrolled will NOT affect the in-flight sequence for that contact — the per-instance audience_attributes snapshot is frozen at enrollment time. Set personalization BEFORE publish, or re-enroll the contact afterward to refresh.

sequence_id.description: The sequence id (uuid) the row belongs to.

contact_id.description: Materialized-row path. Pass when the source has already run and the contact exists in the audience (visible in the builder, returned by the audience-rows endpoint). Mutually exclusive with source_run_id + row_identifier.

source_run_id.description: Staging-row path (use with row_identifier). The source run id from `growth_run_source_preview` output. Numeric string.

row_identifier.description: Staging-row path (use with source_run_id). Each row in the preview output carries a `row_identifier`.

personalization_note.description: The per-recipient line for {{personalization_note}}. Plain text, ≤ 12 words, already vetted by growth_verify_copy. Pass "" to clear.

tools.name: growth_publish_sequence
tools.description: Publish a sequence — flips from draft to active. MUST have been previewed by the user in chat first. Will fail if no connected mailbox / LinkedIn.

tools.name: growth_run_source_preview
tools.description: Run a source preview (sample mode) on an audience source block and wait for the result. Triggers the same Temporal workflow the builder UI fires when you click Preview, then polls until the source run reaches a terminal state and returns the saved preview rows. Intended for iterative prompt / filter work: run the source once, then call growth_run_ai_filter_preview as many times as you want against the saved preview. Returns { source_run_id, status, mode, row_count, rows }. Each row has row_identifier + row_value (the flat contact payload — name, company, enrichments, source-carried fields). Sample preview caps at a small number of contacts so runs finish in seconds; use the web builder for full runs.

source_node_id.description: The source node id to preview. Get it from growth_get_sequence (look for the source block — id starts with "source_").

timeout_seconds.description: Max seconds to wait for preview to finish. Default 180.

force_refresh.description: Force a fresh source pull even if a completed preview already exists on this source. Default false — the tool returns the cached rows from the most recent completed run, which means zero credits and instant return. Set true ONLY when the user says the data is stale or the source config changed.

tools.name: growth_run_ai_filter_preview
tools.description: Run an AI filter prompt against the already-saved source preview (sample mode) and wait for the result. Requires that growth_run_source_preview (or the builder UI) has already run the source — this tool does NOT re-pull the source, it only scores the cached preview contacts. Returns { passed_count, failed_count, prompt_hash, rows } where each row has ai_filter_pass (bool), ai_filter_reason (the evaluator LLM's one-line justification), plus the full flattened contact payload. Use this for iterating on a prompt: call it, read reasons on rejected / accepted rows, adjust the prompt, call again — each iteration is cheap since the source preview is reused.

filter_node_id.description: The filter node id to evaluate. Get it from growth_get_sequence (the block whose type is "filter").

prompt.description: The natural-language ICP prompt to evaluate. Same shape as initial_filter.ai_filter_prompt — INCLUDE + EXCLUDE for both company and contact. This tool only evaluates — it does NOT persist the prompt to the draft. Call growth_update_ai_filter_prompt after you are happy with the prompt to save it to the sequence.

timeout_seconds.description: Max seconds to wait WITHOUT a worker heartbeat before bailing out. NOT a wall-clock timeout — as long as the worker keeps heartbeating (scoring rows, fetching enrichment), polling continues. Only when updated_at stops advancing for this many seconds do we return the partial state. Default 240. Range 30–600.

tools.name: growth_update_ai_filter_prompt
tools.description: Persist an AI filter prompt to the sequence draft so it is visible in the builder. Call this after iterating with growth_run_ai_filter_preview and landing on a prompt you are happy with. Reads the current draft_id and draft_version automatically, then PATCHes the filter node in the draft. Returns the persisted prompt and new draft_version.

filter_node_id.description: The filter node id. Get it from growth_get_sequence (block whose type is "filter").

prompt.description: The final AI filter prompt to save. Must be non-empty.

tools.name: growth_create_organization
tools.description: Create a new Verbiflow workspace (organization) for the current user. Triggers the same onboarding as web signup: starter sequence templates are seeded synchronously, and an `OnboardingPersonalizationWorkflow` runs in the background to personalize them. The caller is added as a member, but the local MCP context (current `org_slug`) is NOT switched — subsequent tool calls keep operating against the workspace you were in before. Use this when the user wants a new workspace, or right before `growth_transfer_sequence` if they need a destination workspace that does not exist yet. Returns `{ org_id, org_slug, viewer_sender_id, starter_template_ids }`.

name.description: Display name for the new workspace, e.g. the company name. 1-120 chars. Shown in the workspace switcher and used as the seed for the slug.

domain.description: Optional company domain (e.g. 'verbiflow.com'). Used by the personalization workflow to research the company and personalize the seeded starter templates. Skip if you do not have a confident domain — the user can fill it in later.

tools.name: growth_transfer_sequence
tools.description: Move a sequence from the caller's current workspace to a target workspace the caller is also a member of. Moves: the sequence definition, all drafts and revisions, the lead lists + contacts attached to it, and the source-run history. Does NOT move: senders / mailbox auth (OAuth tokens are bound to the source org and would collide on UNIQUE(org, channel, identifier) in target — user must reattach senders in target via the builder), and vendor-side resources (Clay tables, Crunchbase saved searches stay in the user's vendor account; if the target workspace has the same vendor connected, configs resolve fine; otherwise sources sit dormant until reconnected). Pre-flight: caller must be a member of both workspaces (else 403 — call `growth_create_organization` first if the target does not exist), and the sequence must be inactive or paused (active sequences refuse to move so in-flight workflows do not straddle the org boundary). Sequence ASSIGNMENTS (workspace members the sequence was assigned to) are cleared because target-org members may differ. Returns `{ ok, sequence_id, target_org_slug, moved_lead_list_ids, moved_source_run_count, note }`.

sequence_id.description: The sequence to move. Must live in the current workspace (the one this MCP session is operating against — see `growth_session_init.auth.org_slug`).

target_org_slug.description: Slug of the destination workspace. Must be one of the workspaces returned by `growth_session_init.auth.workspaces[].slug` for the current user, otherwise the call returns 403. If the target workspace does not exist yet, call `growth_create_organization` first.

tools.name: growth_sandbox_send_test_email
tools.description: Send a real email to the user's own inbox using Flage's shared warmed sandbox sender. Proves sending works before they connect their own mailbox. Subject + body are composed by Claude. Recipient is the user's email. Rate-limited.

to_email.description: The user's own inbox to deliver the test to.

from_name.description: Display name on the From: header. Default: "Flage Demo".

tools.name: growth_verify_copy
tools.description: Stage 1 mechanical gate for a sequence draft. Deterministic regex only — catches em-dashes, banned phrases ("hope you're well", "circling back", "just wanted to"), bracket placeholders ([Sender], [calendar link]), begging in commercial mode ("would love", "worth 15 min", "happy either way"), invented template vars like {{burner_domain}}, missing personalization, over-length subjects/bodies, missing \n\n paragraph breaks, LinkedIn note > 300 chars, signature blocks in body, connection-request-without-branches, branch not last outer step. Fast, cheap, no LLM call. Qualitative review (hook nod test, CTA quality, breakup strength, cohort/proof grounding) is NOT done here — that is the critic-subagent system's job (see the growth skill's critic.md, hook_critic.md, breakup_critic.md, linkedin_critic.md). Returns {overall_score (0-10), rating, pass (bool), critical_count, suggestions, per_step_scores, instructions}. pass is true only when zero criticals AND score ≥ 7. If pass is false, apply suggestions in severity order (critical > high > medium > low) and re-run. When pass=true, hand the draft to the critic subagents in parallel — do NOT skip that stage. sender_context and target_context are accepted for forward-compat but currently unused by the regex pass.

goal_mode.description: Commercial: selling something (signups / demos / revenue) — full begging ban. Feedback: user interviews / advice / early-discovery — humble register OK, begging checks skipped.

steps.description: Sequence steps to verify — same shape as growth_create_sequence_draft.steps.

sender_context.description: Facts about the USER's company, pulled from growth_research_company on the user's own domain + memory. The LLM uses this to catch unsupported claims like "fellow W24" when cohort says W25.

target_context.description: Facts about the TARGET company, pulled from growth_research_company on the target domain. Used to judge whether the hook is actually target-specific and whether cohort/stage framing makes sense.

tools.name: growth_search_domain
tools.description: Check whether a single domain is available to register and what it costs. Returns { available, banned, registration_price, renewal_price }. The price already includes the $3 markup over InboxKit's wholesale price. Use BEFORE growth_create_mailbox_order to confirm the user-picked domain is purchasable.

tools.name: growth_suggest_domains
tools.description: Generate domain suggestions tied to the current workspace name. Backed by an LLM call against the workspace name + company description. Returns up to ~100 candidate domains, each with `available: null` until the user (or growth_search_domain) checks. Cached 14 days per workspace to avoid repeat LLM cost. Already-known-unavailable domains are filtered out of the response. Use this when the user hasn't named a domain yet and wants suggestions; show them the top ~10 and let them pick.

tools.name: growth_list_purchased_domains
tools.description: List the domains this workspace already owns (purchased through Verbiflow), with their existing mailboxes + remaining capacity (max 5 per domain). Use BEFORE growth_create_mailbox_order to check if the user can attach mailboxes to an existing domain instead of registering a new one (cheaper, faster).

tools.name: growth_create_mailbox_order
tools.description:
PAID ACTION — only call after explicit user confirmation. Creates a billing-intent group for one domain + 1–10 mailboxes. The worker fans out InboxKit provisioning + Stripe charges asynchronously. Returns `{order_group_id, intents}` immediately; poll the order-events stream or refresh growth_list_purchased_domains for fulfillment progress.

Required fields:
  - domain: the registered domain. Must match the @-suffix of every mailbox email.
  - is_new_domain: true if domain needs to be registered (adds a domain purchase intent + registration cost). false if domain is already owned by the workspace.
  - registration_years: 1-10. Only meaningful when is_new_domain=true.
  - mailboxes: array of {email, first_name, last_name, platform}. Min 1, max 10. Default platform: GOOGLE.

NOTE on pricing: the backend looks up the domain registration cost from InboxKit at order-creation time (with the standard $3 markup). You do NOT pass `domain_cost` — it is derived server-side. Use growth_search_domain beforehand to show the user the price for confirmation.

Confirm the proposed order with the user BEFORE calling — once submitted the InboxKit provisioning is async and refunds require manual support.

tools.name: growth_apollo_lookup_phone_start
tools.description: Start a phone-number lookup via Apollo using a person's Apollo ID or LinkedIn URL. Apollo delivers phones asynchronously to our webhook (typically within a few minutes), so this returns immediately with `status: "pending"` and identity/firmographic fields. Use `growth_apollo_lookup_phone_status` with the returned `lookup_id` to fetch the phones once delivered. Requires an Apollo API key connected in the Integrations tab. Consumes Apollo phone credits when the webhook delivers.

apollo_id.description: Apollo person ID (e.g. "64a7ff0cc4dfae00013df1a5"). Pass this OR linkedin_url.

linkedin_url.description: LinkedIn profile URL (e.g. "https://www.linkedin.com/in/tim-zheng-677ba010"). Pass this OR apollo_id.

tools.name: growth_apollo_lookup_phone_status
tools.description: Fetch the current status + result of a phone lookup started via `growth_apollo_lookup_phone_start`. Returns `status: "pending"` if Apollo has not yet delivered the phones to our webhook, `"complete"` with `phone_numbers` populated once delivered, or `"failed"` with an error message. Apollo waterfall delivery typically takes seconds to a few minutes; safe to poll every 10–30s.
